- Build result: the always-run focused excerpt test passed; the opt-in full-capture audit (`SCRATCHLAB_RUN_FULL_DVS_NEAR_ZERO_STATE_AUDIT=1`) passed against all 15 full local captures across 5 measured candidates; `python3 scripts/test_capture_pipeline.py` passed 47/47; `git diff --check` passed. Required `scripts/build.sh all` ran 2,260 tests and exited 65 only on the same established unrelated Advanced diagnostics, MIDI learn/receive/clear, and Coach pause failures (8 = 4 tests × 2 configurations); every new near-zero-state test passed in both configurations.
- Follow-up notes: added `DVSNearZeroStateCandidate`, a state machine over the existing `rawPhaseWindows` stream (no production file touched). It enters indeterminate immediately on any window failing a combined phase-margin/correlation/balance/cycle-count bar, but requires several consecutive qualifying same-direction windows to (re)commit — asymmetric hysteresis, easy in, hard out. Baseline reused the already-verified `phaseSteps`/`phaseRuns` helpers, reproducing the phase-continuity audit's established counts exactly. An isolation candidate (only `exitWindows` raised from 1 to 2, every other gate left permissive) already removed 89-100% of the false `start_stop`/`needle_lift`/steady-fixture samples from the consecutive-window requirement alone — but the same mechanism, at that mildest setting, cost `slow_reversals` 55% of its genuine transitions (47→21) and `baby_scratch` 11% (307→274), because genuine fast reversals in these fixtures frequently produce only one raw-decodable window before dropping to dead-band, structurally identical to the false samples' own shape. Adding phase-margin/correlation/balance/cycle-count gates on top removed the residual false content (`start_stop` down to 0 at margin≥20°) but cost sharply more genuine content in `baby_scratch` (down to 90, then 60, then 50) and `fine_flicks` (down to 66, 52, 26). `fast_reversals` stayed comparatively cheap throughout (at most 37% lost). No candidate reached 0% genuine loss on `slow_reversals`/`baby_scratch` at any tested strength, so none beats the previously-tested `nearStopHysteresis` candidate (86% false-removal, 0% loss on those two fixtures) on the genuine-retention axis. This is the fourth independent signal family (displacement, timing/hysteresis, raw phase continuity, and now an explicit indeterminate state) that fails to cleanly separate this false-positive class from genuine fast/fine reversal content using audio-only features. No candidate is recommended for production. Nothing was committed, staged, or pushed.

## 2026-08-01 (Offline-only decoder-level phase-continuity audit — no clean separation found)
- Selected task: Karl directed the next safe DVS investigation directly (not via a ChatGPT plan block) — an offline-only decoder-level phase-continuity audit, since the prior reversal-confirmation audit found no post-decode heuristic (displacement floor, consecutive-window confirmation, near-stop hysteresis, or a combination) could safely separate `start_stop`/`needle_lift`'s false backward samples from genuine reversals without destroying real fast/fine-flick/baby-scratch content.
- Files changed: `ScratchLabDesktopTests/TimecodeFixtureValidationTests.swift` only (new "MARK: - DVS Phase-Continuity Audit" section). `TASKS.md`, `DEV_LOG.md`, `AI_HANDOFF.md`, `AI_HANDOFF/next_prompt.md`.
- Design: duplicated `TimecodePhaseDecoder`'s private `extractPhaseDelta`/`zcrFrequency` math exactly (same silence/clipping/correlation/carrier gates, same ±30° dead band) inside the test file — `TimecodePhaseDecoder.swift` was not touched, since its matching helpers are `private` and loosening that would itself be a production-decoder change. Unlike the real decoder, the audit keeps per-channel phase and classifies every window into `silenceOrClipped`/`lowConfidence`/`deadBand`/`decodable`, computes a best-fit unwrapped phase-step residual between consecutive measurable windows (trying both rotation signs since ZCR frequency carries no sign), then groups the decodable stream into same-direction runs and attaches to each run's first window the entry-step residual and the duration of contiguous non-decodable dwell immediately preceding it.
- Bug caught before trusting any measurement: an early run (before applying the same `invertDirection = true` Rane calibration every other fixture replay in this file already uses via `TimecodePrototypeProfile.raneOneMkiiDebug()`) decoded `position_start/middle/end` — single-carrier 1x-forward captures — as uniformly "backward" against the raw pre-calibration phase math. Confirmed this was a calibration-convention mismatch (not a decoder or math bug) by checking `TimecodePrototypeProfile.swift`, then applied the same inversion the pipeline already applies downstream of the raw decoder; the corrected rerun matched all catalog expectations.
- Measurements (1024-frame window, all 15 full local captures): `start_stop` (42.379s) produced 19 false backward runs (47 raw decodable windows — lower in the pipeline than the previously-established 28 post-stability-filter count, since this audit inspects raw decoder output only, with no stability filter applied); `needle_lift` (44.288s) produced 1 false backward run. Against 492 genuine reversal transitions across `slow_reversals`/`fast_reversals`/`fine_flicks`/`baby_scratch`, no raw phase-continuity measure separated the two: entry-residual spans the same 0–180° range for genuine transitions too (`fast_reversals` genuine transitions range 0.92°–172.86°); correlation for `baby_scratch`'s genuine transitions is often lower than `start_stop`'s false runs (196/307 genuine `baby_scratch` transitions below 0.3 correlation, versus 0.103–0.552 for the 19 `start_stop` false runs); and preceding low-confidence/dead-band dwell overlaps almost completely — 16 of 19 `start_stop` false runs have 0–14 windows of preceding dwell, entirely inside the range genuine `fine_flicks`/`slow_reversals` transitions themselves produce (max 14/11). Only 3 of 19 `start_stop` false runs (dwell 21/39/84 windows) and `needle_lift`'s one false run (257 windows = 5.48s) sit outside that overlap, but those are multi-second silence-adjacent spans a plain duration check would already catch, not evidence specific to phase continuity, and cover only a minority of the false samples.
- Conclusion: raw stereo carrier phase continuity does not cleanly separate genuine reversals from false `start_stop`/`needle_lift` reverses — a true reversal's zero-crossing and a false stop/catch's near-stall moment produce the same low-correlation, low-cycle-count, briefly-incoherent carrier signature. No candidate decision rule was implemented, per the explicit instruction to conclude honestly rather than add another heuristic when the measurements do not support one. The stubborn `start_stop` sample near 12.8s already flagged by the prior audit (survives `nearStopHysteresis` because its velocity is above the floor) shows moderate correlation (0.49), a real measured cycle count (9.26), and near-zero entry residual here too — consistent with a genuine, briefly phase-locked backward carrier (most plausibly the platter physically rebounding at the instant of a hand catch), not decoder noise.
- Build result: the always-run focused excerpt test (`testHardwareTransitionExcerptsReportPhaseContinuityAudit`) passed in both scheme configurations; the opt-in full-capture audit (`testLocalFullHardwareCapturesReportPhaseContinuityAudit`, `SCRATCHLAB_RUN_FULL_DVS_PHASE_CONTINUITY_AUDIT=1` via `launchctl setenv`/`unsetenv`) passed in both configurations against all 15 full local captures; `python3 scripts/test_capture_pipeline.py` passed 47/47; `git diff --check` passed. Required `scripts/build.sh all` ran the full desktop XCTest plan in both test-plan configurations (2,258 tests) and exited 65 only on the same established unrelated Advanced diagnostics, MIDI learn/receive/clear, and Coach pause failures (`set -euo pipefail` stops the script at the test stage before the iOS/macOS/watchOS build legs, the repo's normal behavior whenever these pre-existing failures are present); no new failure appeared and every new phase-continuity test passed in both configurations.
- Follow-up notes: no production decoder, callback size, cadence, stability filter, trust gate, playback, notation routing, visualization, persistence, export, or confidence threshold changed. No further audio-only post-decode heuristic is recommended for this specific false-positive class; closing it would likely need a non-audio signal the app doesn't currently capture live, which is a product decision, not an engineering one, and out of scope here. Nothing was committed, staged, or pushed.

- Build result: focused DVS/timecode suites (`DVSControlVinylAnalyzerTests`, `TimecodeStabilityFilterTests`, `TimecodePrototypeProfileTests`) passed green at every stage of this arc; the required Debug `xcodebuild -project ScratchLab.xcodeproj -scheme ScratchLabDesktop -destination 'platform=macOS,arch=arm64' build` passed at every stage; `git diff --check` passed at every stage; final state pushed to `main` as commits `2f80778`, `28c125f`, `862d3b8` (built on the earlier multichannel-extraction foundation in `cf7953f`, `9f3bd9a`, `6bb2b5c`)
- Follow-up notes: problem was that live Rane ONE MKII (14ch Int32 interleaved @ 48000 Hz) hardware never produced accepted DVS motion, despite synthetic fixtures passing. Diagnosed in stages against real hardware captures rather than assumptions: (1) Auto pair scoring chose 13/14 on raw RMS/peak alone even though it had 0 Hz / 0 zero-crossing-rate on both channels — added a carrier-evidence gate (plausible 500-2500 Hz band plus a minimum zero-crossing rate) so a loud non-carrier pair is rejected as `no timecode carrier`; confirmed live that Auto now selects 5/6 and rejects 13/14. (2) With pair selection fixed, accepted motion was still 0 — root cause was that `TimecodeControlMode.diagnosticsOnly` never runs `TimecodePhaseDecoder` by design; `controlPrototype` mode is required to exercise the actual decoder, and this was not previously understood. (3) In Control Prototype, every frame was still rejected `low_confidence` — the stability filter's confidence gate was hardcoded to 0.3 and never read the UI's `pipeline.minConfidence`; real Rane 5/6 confidence measures around 0.117-0.155, so it could never clear the hardcoded threshold regardless of what the user set in the UI. Wired the gate to the live `minConfidence` value. (4) A user-set Min confidence of 0.10 was then found to silently reset back to the active preset's fixed constant on every relaunch; added persisted override storage and an automatic switch to the existing `.manual` profile whenever the user directly edits calibration, confirmed live that 0.10 now survives relaunch. (5) With motion now decoding, physical forward platter spin reported `backward`; the existing `Invert direction` toggle was already fully wired end-to-end in the decode pipeline and only needed the same relaunch-persistence fix already built for Min confidence — with it enabled, forward spin now correctly reports `forward`. (6) Separately cleaned up and stabilized the DVS control panel's SwiftUI layout (fixed-height rows instead of appearing/disappearing blocks, a collapsed disclosure group for verbose per-channel/per-pair diagnostics) without touching any decoding, calibration, or logger behavior. Final live-validated snapshot on real hardware: signal health `usable`, signal class `quadratureCandidate`, phase offset ≈ -81°, ZCR frequency 986/986 Hz, Min confidence UI/gate 0.100/0.100, frames raw/pre-filter/post-filter 75/74/74, accepted 1382, direction `forward`, raw rate 0.118 u/s, smoothed rate 0.069 u/s, status `usablePrototypeControl`. At no point in this arc was playback, scoring, MIDI, notation routing, or audio output routing enabled or changed — the entire validation stayed within the existing DEBUG-only DVS diagnostics/calibration pipeline.

## 2026-06-18
- Selected task: evidence-driven diagnosis of synthetic quadrature Timecode Prototype live decode instability and CPU load
- Files changed: `ScratchLab/Models/TimecodePhaseDecoder.swift`, `ScratchLab/Models/TimecodeControlPipeline.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktop/Views/MacAnalyzerView.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktopTests/TimecodeDecoderTests.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktopTests/TimecodeLiveTapTests.swift`, `TASKS.md`, `DEV_LOG.md`
- Build result: focused timecode verification passed with `20/20` tests: `xcodebuild -project ScratchLab.xcodeproj -scheme ScratchLabDesktop -destination 'platform=macOS' -only-testing:ScratchLabDesktopTests/TimecodeDecoderTests/testTimecodeDecoderConstantQuadratureProducesNearZeroRate -only-testing:ScratchLabDesktopTests/TimecodeLiveTapTests -only-testing:ScratchLabDesktopTests/TimecodeLiveIntegrationTests/testCountersTrackAcceptedAndDropped test`; `git diff --check` passed; `./scripts/build.sh` passed capture-pipeline fixtures (`47/47`) but failed in the broad `ScratchLabDesktop` XCTest/Swift Testing plan on existing unrelated practice/notation/resource failures, with the final failure list no longer containing timecode tests
- Follow-up notes: direct deterministic decoder feed reproduced the synthetic quadrature instability before the fix, proving the problem was not caused by Serato/FSK and was not only Loopback/AVCapture. Root cause was a decoder analysis-window mismatch plus live-path timing/UI pressure: the phase decoder used dot-product quadrature as if every buffer contained integer 1 kHz carrier cycles, but live-sized 1024-frame buffers at 44.1 kHz do not; the pipeline used wall-clock `Date()` for audio-buffer relative time, so callback/UI jitter inflated decoded rate; and the live callback posted every audio buffer to the main queue while publishing diagnostics on every buffer. Fixed with continuous audio-frame timestamps, least-squares phase fitting over the sine/cosine basis, a small stationary numerical deadband for residual phase velocity, diagnostics publishing throttled to 10 Hz while preserving every decode buffer, pending counter flush on decode, and main-queue callback coalescing. Did not change decoder confidence thresholds, RANE/replay/platter logic, notation/export/schema, app resources, or compatibility claims. Manual Loopback validation is still required for CPU and live status confirmation on hardware.

- Follow-up notes: root cause was the prototype's clean-audio fix going too far toward transport playback: `VirtualPlatterAudio` used `AVAudioPlayer` and `advanceRecord` called `triggerOnce()` after crossing the cue, so the entire `ahhh` kept playing independently even if the user stopped or pulled the record back. - Selected task: restore positive macOS Baby Scratch detector recognition without reopening the silent-buffer or steady-source false-positive paths
- Files changed: `ScratchLabDesktop/Services/MacScratchDetector.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktopTests/CaptureReliabilityPhase1Tests.swift`, `DEV_LOG.md`

- Follow-up notes: the regression was not the new negative-path classifier thresholds by themselves. The strengthened detector could still score a plausible two-burst Baby Scratch window above threshold, but the online `process(samples:)` path never returned that result because it was too dependent on the streaming window collector: pre-attack context was dropped before collection started, short phrases could miss the valid alignment, and the positive fixture itself used flat sine chunks that were weaker than the real burst envelope the classifier expects. Fixed in three narrow steps: changed the positive fixture to use tapered push/pull bursts and added summary assertions proving the fixture produces a passing two-onset window; kept the stricter negative-path guards (`minimumEnergySpan`, lower-but-still-nonzero peak/variance floors) so silence and steady loops still reject; and added a bounded batch-analysis fallback in `MacScratchDetector.process(samples:)` that reuses the same `analyze(...)` classifier when the current call’s samples already contain a valid window but the streaming collector missed it. Also kept a small internal `debugSummaries` utility so tests can assert why the positive fixture is valid instead of only asserting the final label. The full script’s remaining blocker is unrelated to the detector fix: `RoutineSessionDrafts` already exists in a temp session folder during the broader desktop run.

- Follow-up notes: root cause was in `RoutineDetectedNotationBuilder`, not notation drawing. The old builder only observed hand position when `HandMotionState` changed, so a real baby-scratch stroke was often measured from its start to the delayed commit point of the next opposite direction instead of to the furthest excursion reached during that stroke. Those collapsed deltas then failed `RoutineNotationEventNormalizer` thresholds, which explained why long audio phrases still exported only 1-3 movement events. Fixed by having `MacCaptureEngine` feed every published routine-capture hand observation into the builder, tracking each active stroke's latest and furthest confirmed position/time, finishing the stroke at its furthest excursion when direction changes or capture ends, and then starting the next direction from the new committed sample. Preserved the earlier `normalizedRecordDirection(forCameraSpaceDirection:)` source mapping, slightly lowered `minStrokeDuration`, `minPositionDelta`, and `minSpeedForStroke` to keep shorter truthful baby-scratch passes, and added regressions for alternating multi-stroke phrases, direction-change splitting, repetition survival, jitter rejection, and source wiring to `recordObservation`.

The analyzer now emits real `forwardDuration`, `backwardDuration`, and `timingError` values plus `[ScratchMotion]` debug logs, and the synthetic regression cases now prove both the balanced and unbalanced baby-scratch paths. No capture, export, upload, watch, signing, entitlement, or App Store metadata logic changed.

- Selected task: fix confirmed live export blockers for calibration validation and selected-take timing metadata resolution
- Files changed: `ScratchLab/Services/SessionExportCoordinator.swift`, `ScratchLab/Views/CompanionCameraView.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktopTests/CaptureReliabilityPhase1Tests.swift`, `scripts/test_capture_pipeline.py`, `TASKS.md`, `DEV_LOG.md`
- Build result: `xcodebuild -project ScratchLab.xcodeproj -scheme ScratchLabDesktop -destination 'platform=macOS' test -only-testing:ScratchLabDesktopTests/CaptureReliabilityPhase1CoreTests/testCalibrationModeExportMetadataDisablesClickTrack -only-testing:ScratchLabDesktopTests/CaptureReliabilityPhase1CoreTests/testLocalRecordingExportUsesSharedMetadataResolverForClickTrackConfig -only-testing:ScratchLabDesktopTests/CaptureReliabilityPhase1CoreTests/testLocalRecordingExportPrefersSelectedTakeMetadataOverCompatibleSiblingDefaults` passed; `xcodebuild -project ScratchLab.xcodeproj -scheme ScratchLabDesktop -destination 'platform=macOS' test -only-testing:ScratchLabDesktopTests/CaptureReliabilityPhase1CoreTests` passed; `./scripts/build.sh` passed end-to-end on this machine, including the capture-pipeline fixture suite, the full `ScratchLabDesktop` XCTest plan, the iOS app build, and the watchOS build
- Follow-up notes: root cause was twofold. First, local routine export collapsed calibration takes with `bpm = nil` into `take.bpm = 0`, then the shared canonical validator still required every exported take BPM to be inside the timed capture range, which surfaced the generic `This session has inconsistent metadata.` block even though the persisted calibration sidecar was valid. Second, the shared metadata resolver still chose package/session metadata from the first compatible sidecar or an unrelated current session draft instead of preferring the selected take's persisted sidecar, so `session_metadata.json` and `export_metadata.json` could flatten click/timing fields back to defaults or nulls in mixed compatible sessions. The fix keeps calibration metadata nullable in the exported manifests, derives canonical BPM fallback only for the internal archive path, makes the resolver prefer the selected take sidecar and reject mismatched draft configs, and uses the same validated sidecar source when populating per-take manifest metadata. Archive-level regression values now prove: calibration exports `captureMode = calibration_no_click`, `beatEngineMode = silent`, `bpm = null`, `clickEnabled = false`, `beatEnabled = false`, `countInBeats = 4`, `beatsPerBar = 4`, `clickStartHostTime = null`, `recordingStartHostTime = 456`, `clickVersion = scratchlab-click-v1`, and `engineVersion = scratchlab-beat-engine-v1`; timed selected-take exports retain `captureMode = timed_click`, `beatEngineMode = click_track`, `bpm = 95`, `clickEnabled = true`, `beatEnabled = false`, `countInBeats = 4`, `beatsPerBar = 4`, `clickStartHostTime = 55555`, `recordingStartHostTime = 66666`, `clickVersion = scratchlab-click-v1`, and `engineVersion = scratchlab-beat-engine-v1`. Hardware/manual macOS capture verification was not completed in this environment because the real camera/audio/watch relay flow is not available here; the added archive-level tests cover the exact exported manifest fields instead.

- Follow-up notes: traced stages 1–4 by code reading plus new instrumentation, and stages 5–9 by code reading only (no live hardware evidence yet for those). **Stage 1 (measured carrier/phase) is the dominant, architectural latency floor**: `MacCaptureEngine` captures audio via `AVCaptureAudioDataOutput` (the camera/mic-recording pipeline), not a dedicated low-latency `AVAudioEngine` tap, and real hardware buffers observed in prior snapshots were `7168` samples @ 48 kHz ≈ `149 ms` each — meaning any motion change within a single buffer is invisible until the next buffer arrives (≥150 ms floor before any smoothing). This is unrelated to the 60 Hz flush timer, which mostly ticks on empty accumulator windows since buffers arrive far slower than 60 Hz. Changing this would mean swapping the audio capture backend — a broad, risky change out of scope for a traced single-stage fix. **Stage 2/3 (raw decode direction, post-invert) confirmed correct and effectively instantaneous** via new diagnostics: `TimecodeControlCounters.rawDecodeTrace`/`calibratedTrace` (and matching `TimecodeValidationSnapshot` fields "Raw decode (dir/vel)"/"Calibrated (dir/vel)") expose the decoder's actual per-frame direction/velocity before and after invert/rateScale, for the very first time — previously the snapshot's "Rate (raw)" field was a misnomer that actually aliased the same EMA-smoothed value as "Rate (smoothed)" (`decodedRate: currentRate` in `TimecodeControlPipeline.makeValidationSnapshot()`), so there was no way to see genuinely pre-smoothing decoder output at all. New regressions (`testStageTraceShowsRawThenInvertedDirection`, `testRawDecodeTraceShowsReversalWithinOneFlush`) confirm the raw decoder flips direction correctly per-buffer (including within a single flush window spanning a reversal) and that invert cleanly flips the sign with no added smoothing. **Stage 4 (confidence gate + EMA smoothing) is a second, compounding lag source**: `currentDirection`/`currentRate` — the properties that actually drive `TimecodePlaybackBridge`/`TimecodeDriveStepConverter`/playback — are derived from the stability filter's EMA-smoothed rate (`smoothingAlpha: 0.3` default, unconfigurable from the UI), not from the raw per-frame decode. A genuine reversal is accepted immediately by the filter's `isGenuineReversal` bypass, but the EMA itself still needs multiple accepted samples to cross the zero dead-band before `currentDirection` flips — and since new real frames only arrive at the ~150 ms buffer cadence (stage 1) and flushes have shown as few as 3 accepted frames, a fast back-stroke can complete before the EMA ever crosses zero, meaning the reversal may never register in `currentDirection` at all. Stages 1+4 together plausibly explain all five reported symptoms (lag, lost reversals, lost fine/fast motion, and rate/pitch not matching real speed, since `currentRate` is a damped EMA rather than instantaneous velocity). Did not touch dead-band, confidence gate, rate scale, or the EMA itself this slice — per Karl's explicit instruction, no tuning until stages are empirically confirmed on real hardware with the new raw/calibrated trace fields. Added `testConfirmedTrailingReversalFlipsDirectionImmediately`, which establishes a strong, well-converged forward EMA then feeds only 2 backward buffers and asserts `currentDirection` flips immediately (2 frames alone at alpha=0.3 are nowhere near enough to cross a well-converged EMA on their own — this is the actual behavior delta from the old code). The previous slice's fix only flipped `currentDirection`, leaving `currentRate`'s sign to still coast through the EMA — so it had no effect on real playback. Renamed `trailingConfirmedReversalDirection` → `trailingConfirmedReversal`, now returning the confirmed run's mean velocity alongside its direction, and `TimecodeControlPipeline.flushDecode()` now snaps both `currentRate` AND the persisted `stabilityFilterState.smoothedRate` to that value when a reversal is confirmed (not just the direction label) — otherwise the EMA would just coast back toward the old direction on the very next flush. Strengthened `testConfirmedTrailingReversalFlipsDirectionImmediately`/`testSingleTrailingReversalFrameDoesNotFlipDirection` with `currentRate` sign assertions to lock in the property that actually matters. **Then fixed the Stage-0 pair-selection bug** Karl found in the same snapshot (`selected=1/2`, `autoReason=no pair passed validity checks; defaulted to 1/2`) — pair 3/4 momentarily near-silent during a stop/reversal, a real and expected property of velocity-encoded DVS timecode (a genuine platter-velocity zero-crossing produces near-zero carrier amplitude), not a fault. `TimecodeCMSampleBufferAdapter`'s existing `RetentionState`/`updateRetentionState` already had a *partial* fix from an earlier session (a 0.5s time-bounded retention with an RMS floor) but that window is far shorter than a real pause (Karl's snapshot showed a `13898.7 ms` — nearly 14 second — dropout), so it correctly-per-its-own-design expired and fell through to whatever pair scored least-negative. Replaced it with an indefinite-hold model: once Auto acquires a pair, it holds that pair through any silence/invalid buffer, with no time limit and no RMS floor, until a *different* pair shows a meaningfully-better score (`switchScoreAdvantage: Float = 0.05`, chosen against real measured scores clustering 0.3-0.4) sustained across `switchConfirmBufferCount = 5` consecutive buffers (~50 ms at the ~10 ms buffer cadence this tap already documented) — long enough to reject a transient blip on an unrelated channel, short enough to still respond to a genuine, sustained pair change. Also fixed `makeStereoResult`'s `recommended` derivation, which previously only consulted the held pair when the current buffer's `best` score was negative — meaning a transient signal on another pair scoring positive for even one buffer could silently steal selection outright, bypassing the hysteresis state entirely; it now always prefers the held pair (when one exists) regardless of what any other pair scores on that single buffer, so a switch can only happen through the gated `updateRetentionState` path. Diagnostics text changed from "no pair passed validity checks; defaulted to X" to "holding last valid pair X (reason: ...)" whenever the recommended pair equals the held pair and that pair's own score is momentarily negative — false "defaulted" alarms during ordinary stops no longer read as a failure. Added `resetPairRetention()` and wired it to the three reset conditions Karl specified: capture device change (`MacCaptureEngine.reconfigureSession()`), manual selection change (the `channelPairSelection` setter itself, changed-value-gated to avoid redundant resets), and the two DEBUG manual-reset buttons in `TimecodeControlCard` ("Reset Calibration", "Flush + Reset") standing in for an explicit session restart in this DEBUG-testing context. **Added the Rane ONE MKII DEBUG hardware profile**: new `TimecodeControlPreset.raneOneMkiiDebug` / `TimecodePrototypeProfile.raneOneMkiiDebug()` fixing `invertDirection: true`, `minConfidence: 0.10` (both validated against real hardware this session) — the USB channel-pair pin to physical 3/4 is applied by the caller (`TimecodeControlCard.applyPreset`), guarded behind `ENABLE_TIMECODE_LIVE_TAP`, since `TimecodePrototypeProfile` itself is a cross-platform model file that must not assume that macOS-only live-tap capability exists; selecting any other preset restores Auto so the picker stays consistent with what's displayed. Rewrote the retention test block (previously 8 tests exercising the removed time-based-expiry model) with 12 tests covering Karl's 6 pure-logic regressions (acquire, hold-through-silence, hold-indefinitely, carrier-returns-without-switching, transient-doesn't-steal, sustained-switch) plus streak-reset and manual/reset-API coverage, and added a 7th (profile) regression in `TimecodePrototypeProfileTests.swift`. Did not tune the EMA, rate scale, fades, or decoder direction convention in this slice, per Karl's explicit instruction. `TASKS.md` left unchanged/incomplete — needs a fresh hardware relaunch (Rane DEBUG preset, or Auto with the new hysteresis) and a real stop/reversal/scratch test to confirm both this slice's fixes actually resolve the reported symptoms before anything is marked complete.

## 2026-07-31 (continuous DVS grain timing under timer jitter)
- Selected task: make DVS grain timing continuous under real 60 Hz timer jitter
- Root cause: after DVS control moved to its dedicated worker, the playback controller still applied a second exact `1/60`-second wall-clock limiter. Dispatch timer jitter legitimately delivered some ticks slightly early; those calls were rejected after the drive converter had integrated their platter displacement. The next accepted call therefore scheduled accumulated displacement against only the newest tick's segment window, creating an inflated pitch grain and an output hole. Scheduling exactly one elapsed window also left no reserve against ordinary control/audio clock jitter.
- Files changed in this slice: `ScratchLabDesktop/Services/ScratchSamplePlaybackController.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktopTests/ScratchSamplePlaybackControllerTests.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktopTests/TimecodeFixtureValidationTests.swift`, `TASKS.md`, `DEV_LOG.md`, `AI_HANDOFF.md`, `AI_HANDOFF/next_prompt.md`
- Implementation: DVS calls identified by their explicit segment window bypass the unchanged MIDI limiter. DVS elapsed time accumulates across zero-step or otherwise unscheduled updates, is capped at 250 ms, and is consumed/reset only with the matching accumulated step displacement. The scheduler estimates remaining queued output time and restores a 4 ms reserve only when depleted; same-direction grains maintain that bounded reserve, while a reversal interruption rebuilds it once. Physical diagnostic rate remains based on the matched control window. The real-fixture playback harness no longer adds a one-microsecond workaround to pass the former limiter and now accepts variable control intervals.
- Verification: deterministic tests cover 120 alternating 15.5/17.8 ms steady-1x ticks without a discarded grain or catch-up spike, zero-step window accumulation, bounded reserve, and reversal reset. Captured `steady_normal` timecode replays through the production pipeline/bridge/converter/scheduler under the same jitter and stays within 0.85–1.15x. Focused playback and fixture suites passed `112/112`; direct Debug macOS build succeeded; capture-pipeline fixtures passed `47/47`; `git diff --check` passed. Required `scripts/build.sh` completed both configurations and exited code 65 only for the documented unrelated Advanced diagnostics/MIDI/Coach and notation source-contract baseline failures; all edited suites passed.
- Follow-up notes: the 15 saved capture set is sufficient for further decoder, reversal, dropout, position, and scheduler work. Do not request repeated turntable runs; reserve one short hardware listening check for the final output path. MIDI behavior, decoder thresholds, Rane calibration, displacement, capture/export, signing, and entitlements were unchanged. Nothing was committed, staged, or pushed.

## 2026-07-31 (DVS reversal grain handoffs stay continuous; remaining gaps proven decode-driven, not synthesized)
- Selected task: the follow-up hardware listening check after the timer-jitter fix still reported Ahhh sounding "slightly garbled like its under water" during reversals. A DEBUG-only `scheduledGrainObserver` on `ScratchSamplePlaybackController` plus `DVSOfflineGrainRendererTests` (added this arc) replay the saved full-length hardware captures through the unmodified production decode → bridge → step-converter → scheduler path and reconstruct the actual `AVAudioPlayerNode` output offline. That renderer proved `steady_normal` gapless/overlap-free, but `slow_reversals`/`fast_reversals` had 18/36 gaps and 19/45 *interrupted overlaps* — every DVS direction change used `AVAudioPlayerNodeBufferOptions.interrupts`, discarding the bounded queued tail and applying a zero-edge fade, turning every reversal into a deterministic PCM truncation.
- Root cause and fix: `ScratchSamplePlaybackController.positionDidChangeOnQueue` now only applies `.interrupts`/the edge fade for the legacy MIDI reversal path (`dvsWindow == nil`); DVS reversals preserve the existing bounded (~4 ms) queue reserve and enqueue the reversed grain immediately after it, so direction-change latency is bounded by that reserve instead of an audible truncation.
- Files changed in this slice: `ScratchLabDesktop/Services/ScratchSamplePlaybackController.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktopTests/ScratchSamplePlaybackControllerTests.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktopTests/DVSOfflineGrainRendererTests.swift`, `TASKS.md`, `DEV_LOG.md`, `AI_HANDOFF.md`, `AI_HANDOFF/next_prompt.md`
- Investigation of the resulting larger gap totals: removing the interrupt path surfaced more measured "gaps" than before (`slow_reversals`: 36 gaps/3.4520s; `fast_reversals`: 43 gaps/1.2113s) purely because the old interrupts branch never left silence to begin with (it truncates and starts immediately, so it never counted as a gap) — it wasn't actually eliminating the underlying no-drive intervals, just hiding them behind a click. To tell a real scheduling defect apart from expected fail-closed behavior, the offline harness now also records each control tick's `TimecodePlaybackBridge.lastDecision` and the controller's `lastScheduleSkippedReason`, and a new `unexplainedGapDuration` correlates every reported gap interval against those records — a gap only counts as "explained" if every tick inside it is either a non-driving bridge decision (fail-closed: low confidence/unusable signal/stale/missing timeline near a genuine zero-crossing or decode-reacquisition) or a legitimate controller skip (`nearStop`/`tinyGrain`/`noMotion`/`priming`/`noDirection`). Both reversal fixtures report `unexplainedGap=0.0000s` — every millisecond of measured gap time is attributable to the bridge/controller correctly withholding a grain near a genuine platter-velocity zero-crossing, not a scheduling defect. No motion was synthesized over those intervals and none was added; fail-closed behavior is retained exactly as required.
- Verification: `ScratchSamplePlaybackControllerTests` + `DVSOfflineGrainRendererTests` passed `86/86` in both scheme configurations, including `testDVSReversalPreservesTheBoundedQueueCushion` and the new `overlapCount == 0` / `unexplainedGapDuration == 0` regressions on the saved reversal captures; direct Debug macOS build and build-for-testing passed; `python3 scripts/test_capture_pipeline.py` passed `47/47`; `git diff --check` passed. `scripts/build.sh` reproduced exactly the established unrelated baseline failures (`testAdvancedDiagnosticsExplainCameraAndTickActivity`, MIDI learn/clear, `testCoachPauseHoldsPoseFromAudioTimeAndAvoidsPausedTimelineWork`, `CrossPlatformNotationParityTests`, `NotationSheetTests.templateDemoStillOwnsBabyScratchTemplateLabel`) with no new failures, then stopped via its own `set -e` before the iOS/macOS/watch build stages as it always does at this baseline; a direct iOS build (code signing disabled to bypass an unrelated local watch-companion provisioning-profile mismatch, not a code issue) succeeded separately.

## 2026-07-31 (Catmull-Rom fix for static-like clicking in the sub-0.25x DVS software time-stretch path)
- Selected task: Karl's listening comparison of the three offline WAVs found `steady_normal` clean, `fast_reversals` "sounds good," but `slow_reversals` has "static-like clicking" and "does not sound like a natural forward/reverse Ahhh." Added as the new first unchecked task and worked immediately, per instruction not to reconnect the turntable yet.
- Investigation before any code change: extended `DVSOfflineGrainRendererTests` with three independent measurements against the real saved captures, to prove rather than assume where the defect lives.
  1. Grain-boundary PCM value/slope jumps (comparing each scheduled grain's PCM directly against the next): comparable between software-time-stretched-involved boundaries and normal-only boundaries in both `slow_reversals` and `fast_reversals`. Not the differentiator.
  2. Gap-edge click amplitude (the real, legitimate fail-closed silence gaps proven correct in the prior slice are hard cuts with no fade — checked whether the audio bordering them is far from zero): comparable between fixtures, and if anything slightly *worse* in `fast_reversals` (mean 0.160/max 0.553) than `slow_reversals` (mean 0.127/max 0.505) — since `fast_reversals` was reported clean, this rules out gap-edge clicks as the cause too.
  3. Oscillation/high-frequency content ("richness" — a sign-change-rate proxy for how much real waveform detail a grain's PCM retains): software-time-stretched grains measured systematically lower than normal grains in *every* fixture (`fast_reversals`: 462.7/sec vs 4606.4/sec normal, roughly a 10x drop; `steady_normal` has zero software-slow grains at all). The decisive fact distinguishing the two reversal fixtures: `slow_reversals` spends ~38% of all its grains on the software-stretch path (781/2073) versus only ~6% for `fast_reversals` (75/1180) — the same underlying quality gap exists in both, but only dominates the perceived character where it happens this often.
- Root cause and fix: `ScratchSamplePlaybackController.copyTimeStretched` reconstructed a stretched grain with plain linear interpolation between the two raw samples surrounding each output position — with as few as 2-9 real raw samples stretched across a ~735-frame output window at extreme speed ratios, this collapses much of the true waveform's curvature into straight-line segments. Fixed by switching to Catmull-Rom cubic interpolation (using one additional real sample of context on each side, already present in the copied segment — no wider source read, no change to needle position/frame accounting) whenever at least 4 raw source frames are available; grains with only 2-3 raw frames keep the original linear method, since there is no additional real information for a cubic fit to use there.
- Files changed in this slice: `ScratchLabDesktop/Services/ScratchSamplePlaybackController.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktopTests/ScratchSamplePlaybackControllerTests.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktopTests/DVSOfflineGrainRendererTests.swift`, `TASKS.md`, `DEV_LOG.md`, `AI_HANDOFF.md`, `AI_HANDOFF/next_prompt.md`
- Measured improvement (real fixture, before/after): `slow_reversals` software-slow-grain richness rose from 601.0/sec to 648.5/sec; `fast_reversals` rose from 462.7/sec to 506.3/sec. This is real but modest (~8-9%) — the smallest change the measurement actually justified, not a guaranteed complete fix. `testOfflineRenderReconstructsSlowReversalsCapture` now asserts a richness floor (620/sec) on the real fixture that would fail if a future change regressed back toward plain-linear's measured 601/sec baseline. `testDVSSoftwareTimeStretchUsesCubicInterpolationNotPlainLinear` (new, in `ScratchSamplePlaybackControllerTests`) independently re-derives what plain linear interpolation would have produced for a real scheduled grain from the bundled `ahhh.wav` asset and proves the observed output differs from it — a determinism check independent of any fixture.
- Verification: `ScratchSamplePlaybackControllerTests` + `DVSOfflineGrainRendererTests` passed `87/87` in both scheme configurations; direct Debug macOS build and build-for-testing passed; a direct iOS build (code signing disabled to bypass the same unrelated local watch-companion provisioning-profile mismatch noted in the prior slice) succeeded; `python3 scripts/test_capture_pipeline.py` passed `47/47`; `scripts/build.sh` reproduced exactly the established unrelated baseline (Advanced diagnostics, MIDI learn/clear, Coach pause, notation source-contract) with no new failures before stopping via its own `set -e`; `git diff --check` passed.
- Follow-up notes: needle position/frame accounting, direction logic, decoder thresholds, Rane calibration, and the reversal queue-handoff fix from the prior slice are all byte-for-byte unchanged. The three offline WAVs (including the regenerated `slow_reversals`) are at the same sandboxed container path as before for Karl's next listen. No hardware/turntable time was requested. Nothing was committed, staged, or pushed.

- `TimecodeNotationTrustGate`: a stateless, side-effect-free `evaluate(...)` mirroring `TimecodePlaybackBridge.evaluate`'s exact 8-gate order and thresholds (mode, replay conflict, live tap, signal health, staleness, confidence, timeline presence, direction, validation) — verified never to read or touch `playbackDriveEnabled`, and `TimecodePlaybackBridge` itself was not modified at all. `notationRoutingEnabled` is a plain parameter the caller passes in, not a stored setting.

Confidence and position are carried through unchanged (never averaged/boosted). Since it only ever appends real samples from windows the caller passes it, a real gap between two appended windows (the trust gate having rejected the interval in between) survives untouched as a real time jump — proven directly by `testAccumulatorDoesNotSynthesizeSamplesAcrossAGap`.

Only `.directionSegment` primitives become events; idle holds and reversals are not emitted as their own movement events, matching the plan.

Assertions were scoped to what each excerpt's length actually supports (at least one real, correctly-tagged event for the reversal/flick excerpts; both directions for the longer `baby_scratch` excerpt, which does clear that bar) rather than weakened arbitrarily, with the reasoning documented directly in the test file.

## 2026-07-31 (DVS notation slice 5 — final hardware validation)
- Selected task: Karl confirmed starting slice 5, the final slice of the recorded DVS-to-notation routing plan — one real session with a physical Rane ONE MKII to confirm notation routing behaves correctly end-to-end on live hardware.
- Since I have no way to operate physical DJ hardware, added a temporary, uncommitted, `#if DEBUG` env-var check to `MacAnalyzerView.onAppear` (`SCRATCHLAB_ENABLE_DVS_NOTATION`) that flips `notationRoutingEnabled` on for one launch only, without touching the stored property's own default (`false`) — every other debug run and every XCTest run stayed unaffected. Karl launched the app with that env var set, connected his physical Rane ONE MKII using the same timecode-vinyl rig already used to capture the slices 1–4 fixtures, got the Setup Checklist fully green (including "Validation passed"), and recorded 3 routine takes of real baby-scratch motion via the normal Routine Capture Start Recording control — the exact retry an earlier, partial hardware attempt (recorded in `TASKS.md`'s slice 5 entry before this session, from a separate agent run) had identified as still needed.
- Result: all 3 exported takes (`session_2026_07_31_unknown_performer_baby_scratch_95_bpm`, 18.3s/14.4s/26.9s) showed `detectionSources: ["audio", "timecode_live"]` and real, correctly alternating forward/backward `recordMovementEvents` (10/14/17 events) — DVS notation routing worked end-to-end on live hardware, trust-gated and validated exactly as designed, with playback override left independently off throughout.
- Bug found via this real session, exactly what slice 5 exists to catch: every individual `recordMovementEvents[].source` in the export read `"video"`, despite the snapshot-level `detectionSources` correctly showing `"timecode_live"`. Root cause: `RoutineNotationFusionEngine.fuseMovementEvents` (`MacCaptureEngine.swift`) unconditionally rebuilds every motion event it emits with a hardcoded `source: "video"` (unmatched events) or `"fused"` (events paired with a burst audio event), discarding whatever source the input event actually carried — a pre-existing assumption baked in before DVS notation existed, when camera was the only possible motion source. Slice 3's `withTimecodeLiveMovementProvenance()` only ever patched the top-level `detectionSources` label, never each event's own `.source` field — invisible to every slice 1–4 test, since all of them exercised precedence/provenance directly and never through the real `RoutineNotationFusionEngine().snapshot(...)` call path production actually uses.
- Fix: extended `CaptureCore.DetectedNotationSnapshot.withTimecodeLiveMovementProvenance()` to also retag every event in `recordMovementEvents` to `source: "timecode_live"` — still a pure, additive post-processing method; `RoutineNotationFusionEngine`'s own internals remain untouched. Safe because the method's only call site (`notationRoutingEnabled && lastDrainedTimecodeNotationTimeline != nil`) guarantees every event in that snapshot originated from DVS, never camera. Updated `testWithTimecodeLiveMovementProvenanceReplacesVideoNotAudio` to assert the corrected behavior. Karl's already-captured session did **not** need to be redone — the bug was purely a mislabeled provenance string, not a data-correctness issue; direction/timing/position data was always correct, confirmed independently via `session_review.json`'s `directionConflictDetected: false` and sane `directionFlipCount` values (8/11/15) across all 3 takes.

Left untouched per instruction; verified it doesn't conflict with this slice's fix.

## 2026-08-01 (Offline-only stop-transition reversal-confirmation rule measured — no candidate proven safe)
- Selected task: Karl approved the next safe DVS investigation queued in `AI_HANDOFF.md` — design and measure an offline-only stop-transition reversal-confirmation rule against the saved hardware fixtures, without changing production cadence or thresholds. This follows directly from the established finding that all 27 video-covered backward samples in `start_stop` at 1024 frames are false (record moving clockwise, caught/held, or restarting clockwise) and that confidence alone cannot separate them (false confidence reaches 0.801).
- Files changed: `ScratchLabDesktopTests/TimecodeFixtureValidationTests.swift` only (new "MARK: - 31." section). `TASKS.md`, `DEV_LOG.md`, `AI_HANDOFF.md`, `AI_HANDOFF/next_prompt.md`.
- Design: a test-only `DVSReversalConfirmationCandidate` enum models each candidate as a small state machine over the already-decoded, already-known-direction 1024-frame stream — a pending direction change is buffered and only "confirmed" (emitted) once it satisfies the candidate's rule; if the pending run reverts to the previously confirmed direction first, it is discarded entirely. `.none` is a baseline that confirms immediately, reproducing today's unfiltered 1024-frame output exactly. `minimumReverseDisplacement` requires the pending run's cumulative `|deltaPosition|` to clear a threshold; `consecutiveWindowConfirmation` requires a minimum consecutive-frame run length; `nearStopHysteresis` excludes any frame below a velocity floor from ever entering the state machine (neither confirming nor breaking the current direction); `combinedNearStopAndConsecutive` applies the floor first, then the consecutive-window rule to the survivors. A shared `decodeDVSFrameStream` helper decodes each fixture once at the established 1024-frame candidate window, so the (expensive) decode cost is paid once per fixture and every candidate is evaluated cheaply against the same decoded stream.
- Bug caught during this slice, before any measurement was trusted: the first version of `decodeDVSFrameStream` discarded `flushDecode()`'s return value and read `pipeline.latestDecodeResult?.frames` unconditionally every window, instead of gating on `flushDecode()` returning non-nil the way the already-validated `auditDVSSubwindow` does. Because `latestDecodeResult` is not cleared on a quiet window, this silently re-appended stale frames from the last successful window on every subsequent quiet window. It inflated `start_stop`'s raw backward count from the established 28 to 310 in the first full-capture run. Caught by cross-checking the new audit's `rawFalse`/`rawChanges` fields against the already-established `DVS_SUBWINDOW` baseline for the same fixtures (28 false in `start_stop`, 1 false in `needle_lift`) before treating any candidate result as real; fixed to gate on `flushDecode()`'s own return value, matching `auditDVSSubwindow` exactly; the corrected rerun reproduced the established raw counts precisely.
- Measurements (1024-frame window, four non-baseline candidates against the full local captures): `minReverseDisplacement(0.15)` fully removes every false reverse in `start_stop` (28/28) and `needle_lift` (1/1) and clears the small pre-existing false blips in the steady/one-way fixtures, but destroys 62-79% of genuine direction changes in `slow_reversals` (45→17), `fine_flicks` (76→16), and `baby_scratch` (292→72) — real fast/fine reversals are frequently just as small in per-frame displacement as the false `start_stop` ones, so a single displacement threshold cannot separate them. `consecutiveWindows(2)`/`(3)` are simultaneously too weak where needed (2/28 and 6/28 `start_stop` false samples removed) and too destructive where it matters (`slow_reversals` genuine changes fall from 45 to 19, a 58% loss) because discarding brief single-frame runs merges adjacent same-direction output and silently collapses pairs of genuine short back-and-forth changes. `nearStopHysteresis(0.15)` alone is the best-preserving candidate for genuine content (0% change loss in `slow_reversals` and `baby_scratch`, at most 8% elsewhere, and zero added latency since it never delays confirmation) and removes 86% of `start_stop`'s false reverses (28→4), but the residual `start_stop` sample at 12.821s and `needle_lift`'s lone false sample both carry velocity above the floor and pass through unchanged. `combined(floor=0.15, windows=2)` closes the `needle_lift` gap completely but reintroduces the `consecutiveWindows` fragmentation cost on top of the floor — `slow_reversals` drops back to the same 58%-loss level and `baby_scratch` loses 18% (292→238) — for no additional `start_stop` benefit over near-stop alone. Position-integration error scales with how much real motion each candidate discards: 0.003-0.03 for the gentlest candidates up to 5.06 for `minReverseDisplacement` on `baby_scratch`. Added confirmation latency is zero for the near-stop-only candidate, tens of milliseconds for `consecutiveWindows`, and up to ~0.64s worst case for `minReverseDisplacement` on `slow_reversals` and ~1.4s for `consecutiveWindows(3)` inside `start_stop`'s long false-hold bursts — both far too slow for responsive scratch feedback even where they do help. Decode/processing cost is unaffected by any candidate (0.033x-0.26x captured duration across all 15 fixtures, matching the already-established 1024-frame baseline); candidate evaluation itself is a negligible O(n) pass over the shared decoded stream.
- Conclusion: no single candidate, and no narrow combination tested, is safe to propose as a production slice. `nearStopHysteresis` is the only one whose genuine-content cost looks tolerable on its own, but it still misses `needle_lift` entirely and 4 of 28 `start_stop` false samples, so closing the remaining gap needs a materially different or supplementary signal rather than a blunter consecutive-window/displacement gate layered on top. No production filter was implemented; no live decoding path, cadence, or threshold was changed, per the explicit scope of this investigation.
- Verification: the always-run excerpt test (`testHardwareTransitionExcerptsReportReversalConfirmationCandidates`, the 6 checked-in 0.24s transition fixtures) passed in both scheme configurations. The opt-in full-capture audit (`testLocalFullHardwareCapturesReportReversalConfirmationCandidates`, gated on `SCRATCHLAB_RUN_FULL_DVS_REVERSAL_CONFIRMATION_AUDIT=1`) passed in both scheme configurations against all 15 full local captures x 6 candidates (90 measurements per pass, 180 total). Getting the full-capture pass to actually see the opt-in env var required `launchctl setenv`/`launchctl unsetenv` rather than a plain shell `export`: the macOS-destination test host is launched through Launch Services (visible as the `RegisterWithLaunchServices` build step), which does not inherit the invoking shell's exported environment. `python3 scripts/test_capture_pipeline.py` passed 47/47. `git diff --check` passed. `scripts/build.sh all` ran both configurations and stopped only on the established unrelated Advanced diagnostics, MIDI learn/receive/clear, Coach pause, and notation source-contract baseline failures, with no new failures.
- Follow-up notes: this was measurement only — no production filter, decoder, threshold, playback, routing, or export behavior changed anywhere. The new audit's log format (`DVS_REVERSAL_CONFIRM label=... candidate=... window=1024 duration=...s raw=...(f.../b...)(...Hz) rawChanges=... rawFalse=... confirmed=...(f.../b...)(...Hz) confirmedChanges=... confirmedFalse=... falseRemoved=... rejected=... latencyMean=...s latencyMax=...s positionErr=... spike=... held=... long=... processing=...s realtimeRatio=...`) follows the same convention as the existing `DVS_DENSITY`/`DVS_SUBWINDOW` audits so future sessions can add further candidates without re-deriving the harness. Nothing was committed, staged, or pushed.

## 2026-08-01 — Clean-room DVS signed-rate excursion stabilizer complete (uncommitted)

- Selected task: add a pure, platform-agnostic signed-rate excursion stabilizer before the two existing unchecked product/future-hardware decisions. No equivalent task existed, and this was the first small implementation-ready task explicitly requested.
- Root cause: continuously sampled signed rate retains genuine reversal timing even while absolute position is unlocked, but its raw sign chatters near zero. The repository had no isolated state machine that could preserve the committed direction while accumulating only a pending opposite-direction excursion, so a direct sign consumer would either duplicate chatter reversals or require an unsafe position-lock gate.
- Files changed: `ScratchLab/Models/TimecodeSignedRateExcursionStabilizer.swift` (new shared pure logic), `ScratchLabDesktopTests/TimecodeSignedRateExcursionStabilizerTests.swift` (new deterministic tests), `ScratchLab.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` (shared iOS/macOS source membership and test membership), `TASKS.md`, `DEV_LOG.md`, `AI_HANDOFF.md`, and `AI_HANDOFF/next_prompt.md`.
- Implementation: explicit `.available`/`.noSignal`/`.unknown` samples carry a finite non-negative timestamp and normalized signed rate. The stabilizer keeps committed and pending directions separate, integrates consecutive opposite-direction magnitude with the trapezoidal rule over actual elapsed time, commits exactly once at `reversalAreaThreshold`, cancels pending evidence when the rate returns to the committed direction, and never accepts or consults position lock. `reversalAreaThreshold` and `maximumIntegrationGap` are injected configuration with no hidden production default. Non-finite/negative/non-monotonic input, invalid configuration, unavailable signal, and excessive gaps clear pending/timing evidence without changing the last committed direction or synthesizing live motion across the discontinuity.
- Scope: no call site was added. `TimecodePhaseDecoder`, `TimecodeControlPipeline`, live capture, playback, notation, export, persistence, UI, and App Store behavior are unchanged. No external/GPL code, headers, constants, translated logic, or linked material entered the repository. This does not claim to fix baby-scratch sound.
- Verification: focused `TimecodeSignedRateExcursionStabilizerTests` passed 10/10 in each of the two test-plan configurations (20 executions). Existing DVS-adjacent decoder/stability/live-tap/live-integration/validation/fixture/bridge/profile/analyzer/notation/playback/offline-renderer suites passed 388 executions with 6 expected environment-gated skips and no failures. `python3 scripts/test_capture_pipeline.py` passed 47/47. Required `scripts/build.sh all` ran both configurations; the new tests passed twice, and the script stopped before platform build legs only on the documented established baseline: `testAdvancedDiagnosticsExplainCameraAndTickActivity`, MIDI receive/learn/clear tests, `testCoachPauseHoldsPoseFromAudioTimeAndAvoidsPausedTimelineWork`, `CrossPlatformNotationParityTests.notationCanvasUsesSharedRenderer`, and `NotationSheetTests.templateDemoStillOwnsBabyScratchTemplateLabel`. Direct signed macOS, unsigned iOS (including watch dependency), and unsigned watchOS builds all succeeded afterward. `git diff --check` passed.
- Follow-up: the stabilizer remains intentionally disconnected until a separately scoped, lawful clean-room dense signed-rate estimator is designed and measured. Nothing was committed, staged, pushed, reset, or discarded.

## 2026-08-05 (Diagnose and fix `CaptureReliabilityPhase1CoreTests.testClearCrossfaderMappingRemovesMapping` — uncommitted)

- Selected task: the last remaining item of the "MIDI learn/receive/clear" established-baseline bucket that is actually fixable this session — `testClearCrossfaderMappingRemovesMapping` (`ScratchLabDesktopTests/CaptureReliabilityPhase1Tests.swift:11085`), which persists a `CrossfaderCCMapping` into `UserDefaults.standard`, constructs a `MacCaptureEngine(autoRefreshDevices: false)`, asserts `engine.crossfaderCCMapping` is non-nil (i.e. the persisted mapping was restored), then calls `clearCrossfaderMapping()` and asserts the `UserDefaults` key is gone.
- Root cause, confirmed by reading the full test, `MacCaptureEngine`'s init/`configureInitialState()`/`startDeviceDiscoveryAfterViewMount()`/`clearCrossfaderMapping()`, and `git show`/`git log -S` on the relevant symbols — **a genuine production regression, not a stale test, not UserDefaults contamination, and not a timing/observation issue in the test itself**. Empirically reproduced first: the failure is exactly `XCTAssertNotNil(engine.crossfaderCCMapping)` at line 11094 — `clearCrossfaderMapping()` itself works correctly (`UserDefaults.standard.removeObject(forKey:)` runs synchronously, so the second assertion never fails). Traced with `git log -S"startDeviceDiscoveryAfterViewMount"` to the single commit that introduced it, `026c072` ("macOS: stabilize Rane scratch sample playback", 2026-06-26). Before that commit, `configureInitialState()` decoded a persisted `CrossfaderCCMapping` from `UserDefaults` and set `crossfaderCCMapping`/`midiLearnState` **synchronously**, in the same statement as the still-present `persistedCrossfaderMapping = mapping` line. That commit moved the `crossfaderCCMapping`/`midiLearnState` assignment out of `init` and into the new `startDeviceDiscoveryAfterViewMount()` — an `async` method gated behind `autoRefreshDevicesAfterViewMount` (== the `autoRefreshDevices` init parameter) that also does `await Task.yield()` before publishing. The test constructs its engine with `autoRefreshDevices: false` specifically to stay synchronous/deterministic, which now means `startDeviceDiscoveryAfterViewMount()`'s early `guard autoRefreshDevicesAfterViewMount else { return }` always exits immediately — and even for `autoRefreshDevices: true` callers, nothing in this unit-test context ever calls the `async` method at all, so `crossfaderCCMapping` never gets restored. Critically, `026c072`'s own `DEV_LOG.md` entry (committed in the same commit) states the selected task was narrowly "a fix for `ScratchSamplePlaybackController.loadOnQueue` / `ensureEngineRunning`" after a brace-matching bug left that unrelated controller failing to compile, and its follow-up notes describe only `ScratchSamplePlaybackController.swift` changes — the `MacCaptureEngine.swift` device-discovery-deferral restructuring (visible in the actual commit diff, 185 lines) is never mentioned. This is strong evidence the crossfader-mapping-restore regression was an unintentional side effect swept into that commit alongside legitimately-scoped async deferral of the genuinely expensive `rescanRoutineCaptures()`/`refreshDevices()` device I/O calls, not a deliberate architecture decision — so restoring the historical synchronous behavior for this one cheap, non-I/O UserDefaults decode does not require a product/architecture decision.
- Files changed: `ScratchLabDesktop/Services/MacCaptureEngine.swift` only, inside `configureInitialState()`. Two lines added back exactly where they were before `026c072` removed them:
  ```swift
  if let data = UserDefaults.standard.data(forKey: ScratchLabDesktopDefaultsKey.crossfaderMIDIMapping),
     let mapping = try? JSONDecoder().decode(CrossfaderCCMapping.self, from: data) {
      crossfaderCCMapping = mapping
      midiLearnState = .learned(mapping)
      persistedCrossfaderMapping = mapping
  }
  ```
  The legitimately-intentional async deferral of `rescanRoutineCaptures()`/`refreshDevices()` in `startDeviceDiscoveryAfterViewMount()` was left untouched, including its own (now redundant but harmless/idempotent) re-assignment of the same mapping value for `autoRefreshDevices: true` callers whose view actually invokes that method — removing that redundant block was judged out of scope for "the smallest deterministic correction." No test file changed.

## 2026-08-05 (Diagnose the paired `testMIDILearnUpdatesFromListeningToLearnedStateWhenCCArrives` / `testReceivingMIDICCUpdatesLastMIDIEventSummary` failures — fix the first, stop before the second — uncommitted)

- Selected task: diagnose both previously-unresolved MIDI-CC-reception baseline failures and determine whether they share one root cause. They do not: empirically reproduced both individually and found two entirely distinct failure signatures, so per this task's own instruction ("select the first independently fixable defect, and stop before addressing the second") only `testMIDILearnUpdatesFromListeningToLearnedStateWhenCCArrives` (the first-listed) was fixed this session.
- Diagnosis — `testMIDILearnUpdatesFromListeningToLearnedStateWhenCCArrives` (**genuine production regression, fixed**): the empirical failure was a single assertion — `midiLearnFeedback` expected `"Learned Xfader: CC11 Ch2"` but got `"Received CC11 Ch2 Value64"` — while `crossfaderCCMapping`, `midiLearnState`, and `lastMIDIEventSummary` all already passed, proving the test's `RunLoop.main.run(until:)` spin correctly flushes the async publish path (ruling out main-thread publication timing as the defect) and that this was a pure state-ordering bug. Traced with `git log -S"if isMidiLearn {"` to the single commit that introduced it, `103b613` ("macOS: suspend live input on Review tab", 2026-06-17). Confirmed via `git show 103b613^:...` that the pre-existing code checked `if self.midiLearnState == .listening { self.midiLearnFeedback = summary }` **freshly, inside** the async-dispatched closure — so if an earlier-enqueued closure (from `applyLearnedCrossfaderMapping`, called synchronously earlier in the same `recordReceivedMIDICCEvent` invocation when a mapping was just learned) had already flipped `midiLearnState` to `.learned(...)` by the time this closure ran, the fresh check correctly no-opped and preserved the specific "Learned Xfader: ..." message. Commit `103b613` (whose stated purpose was adding MIDI-monitor UI-publish throttling while Review is active, unrelated to this specific protection) replaced that fresh check with a pre-computed `isMidiLearn` local captured *before* either closure had run — so by the time the monitor-publish closure executed (always second, since `applyLearnedCrossfaderMapping`'s own `publishOnMainAsync` call is enqueued first in the same function), it unconditionally overwrote the correct "Learned Xfader: ..." feedback with the generic "Received CC..." summary on the very event that had just committed the mapping. Confirmed `recordReceivedMIDICCEvent` is the exact real production seam (not a synthetic-only stub): the live CoreMIDI callback chain (`MIDIInputPortCreateWithBlock` → `receiveMIDIPacketList` → the same `applyLearnedCrossfaderMapping`/`recordReceivedMIDICCEvent` call pair for CC status bytes) exhibits the identical ordering, so this was also a real, user-visible UI bug in production (a successful crossfader MIDI-learn gesture would show the generic "Received CC..." caption instead of confirming "Learned Xfader: ..."), not merely a test artifact — no new injection seam was needed since the existing seam already matches the real callback path exactly.
- Diagnosis — `testReceivingMIDICCUpdatesLastMIDIEventSummary` (**test-seam defect, NOT fixed this session, evidence only**): all four assertions fail simultaneously with completely-unset default values (`midiEventsReceivedCount` "0", `lastMIDICCMessage` "CC -- Ch -- Value --", `lastMIDIEventSummary` "No MIDI received yet", `midiListeningState` "Not Connected") — meaning the `publishOnMainAsync`/`DispatchQueue.main.async` closure never ran at all before the assertions executed. Unlike the paired test above, this test calls `recordReceivedMIDICCEvent(...)` and asserts immediately, with **no** `RunLoop.main.run(until:)` spin at all (contrast with `testMIDILearnUpdatesFromListeningToLearnedStateWhenCCArrives`, `testMIDILearnStateTransitionsToListening`, and `testCancelMIDILearnReturnsToIdle`, which all spin the run loop after the async-publishing call and pass). This points to a missing use of the already-established, already-proven-deterministic test seam (`RunLoop.main.run(until:)`) in this one test, not a production defect — but per this task's explicit scope ("select the first independently fixable defect, and stop before addressing the second"), this was diagnosed and left unfixed for a future task.
- Files changed: `ScratchLabDesktop/Services/MacCaptureEngine.swift` only, inside `recordReceivedMIDICCEvent`'s throttled `publishOnMainAsync(field: "midiMonitor", ...)` closure. One line changed (plus an explanatory comment) — restores the pre-`103b613` semantics exactly:
  ```swift
  if self.midiLearnState == .listening {
      self.midiLearnFeedback = latestSummary
  }
  ```

## 2026-08-13 (Fix click-assisted routine capture audio-packet stack overflow)

- Selected task: fix the user-reported crash when recording a Baby Scratch with a click. This superseded the remaining approval-gated DVS tasks because capture reliability is the project's highest priority and the crash report supplied a concrete implementation-ready failure.
- Root cause: `ScratchLab-2026-08-13-193719.ips` reports `Thread stack size exceeded` on the `scratchlab.mac.capture.audio` queue. The faulting stack is `MacCaptureEngine.processAudioSampleBuffer(_:)` → `MacCaptureEngine.audioPacket(from:)` → `IndexingIterator.next()` while converting integer PCM. `audioPacket(from:)` used `AudioBuffer.mDataByteSize / bytesPerSample` as the Range bound, so inconsistent or oversized buffer metadata could produce an effectively unbounded conversion loop on the capture worker. The report proves the audio extraction failure; it does not prove the click generator itself was defective.
- Files changed: `ScratchLabDesktop/Services/MacCaptureEngine.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktopTests/CaptureReliabilityPhase1Tests.swift`, `TASKS.md`, and `DEV_LOG.md`. Existing unrelated notation/design changes were preserved.
- Implementation: added a bounded, overflow-checked `validatedAudioSampleCount` derived from `CMSampleBufferGetNumSamples` and each validated buffer's channel count. Buffer byte size now only proves that the required bytes exist; it no longer controls iteration. The extractor rejects zero or excessive frame/channel counts, unsupported PCM layouts, short buffers, and inconsistent interleaved/non-interleaved buffer layouts before reading memory. Int16/Int32 conversion now uses explicit bounded loops. Existing Float32 and mono-downmix behavior remains unchanged.
- Verification: the changed desktop target compiled. Four focused regressions passed 4/4 in both configured test runs: existing two-buffer non-interleaved Float32 downmix, oversized byte metadata bounded to authoritative frames, inconsistent/excessive metadata rejection, and Rane-style 14-channel interleaved Int32 downmix. `scripts/build.sh` passed capture-pipeline fixtures 47/47, then completed its broad desktop plan with established unrelated failures in removed-resource/scheme assertions, MIDI learn, sample playback, and the pre-existing dirty notation lane-label assertion; none of the new audio tests failed. `git diff --check` passed. An Address Sanitizer build compiled, but repeated locked-device/CoreAudio test-host service errors interrupted it before a valid result bundle was written, so it is not claimed as a pass.
- Remaining risk and verification: only a real capture can prove the exact hardware packet that caused the crash is now rejected or converted safely. Relaunch the rebuilt app, record 10–15 seconds first without a click and then with the click, and confirm both takes finalize and Review opens. If another crash occurs, preserve the new `.ips` report for comparison. Nothing was staged, committed, or pushed.

- Implementation: `BuilderAdmissionGate` shares one `NSLock` for `open`/`admit`/`close`/`isCurrent`; `admit` atomically checks open + `enter()` and returns a generation-tied token; `finalizeRoutineRecording` closes admission first (so later `enter()`s are impossible) then `wait()`s, drains the captured builder with the recorded `finalizationHostTime`, and freezes the trace. A task whose generation is no longer current never mutates the builder.

## 2026-08-14 (Capture-movement loss — deadlock fix: async finalization; uncommitted)

- Selected task: fix the hardware-reproduced finalization deadlock. A live sample showed `fileOutput(didFinishRecordingTo:)` (delivered on the main dispatch queue) → `finalizeRoutineRecording` → `builderAdmissionGate.close().wait()`, which blocked the main queue so the admitted `@MainActor` builder tasks could never run to `leave()` the group.
- Root cause: a synchronous `DispatchGroup.wait()` on the AVFoundation completion/main queue while the group's tasks require MainActor.

## 2026-08-14 (Controller CC6 platter telemetry as primary movement source; uncommitted)

- Selected task: make direct RANE ONE MKII CC6 platter telemetry the preferred record-movement source (camera is a fallback/diagnostic), and fix the two known Release blockers. The 2026-08-14 export proved camera motion is unusable here (266 observations → 238 idle → 1 movement event) while CC6 carries a clean alternating 90-BPM Baby Scratch stream.
- Root cause: `withMixerMidiEvents` only derives FADER events from `mappedControl == "crossfader"`; CC6 platter (`controller 6`) has `mappedControl == nil`, so 8,656 events were persisted but never converted to `recordMovementEvents`. The fusion hardcodes movement provenance as `"video"`.
- Files changed: `ScratchLab/Models/CaptureCore.swift` (`derivePlatterMovementEvents` decoder + `withControllerMovementProvenance`), `ScratchLabDesktop/Services/MacCaptureEngine.swift` (decode CC6 in finalization, prefer controller over camera/DVS, gate `lowLatencyTimecodeTapHasRequiredChannels` to DEBUG), `ScratchLabDesktop/Views/MacAnalyzerView.swift` (truthful "Controller platter"/"DVS timecode" source labels), `ScratchLabDesktop/Services/ScratchSamplePlaybackController.swift` (Release fix: `accumulatedStepsBeforeThisTick` moved out of `#if DEBUG`), `ScratchLabDesktopTests/CaptureReliabilityPhase1Tests.swift` (`ControllerPlatterDecoderTests`, 7 tests), `DEV_LOG.md`.
- Decoder: modular signed deltas (±half modulus) so 127↔0 never false-reverses; integrates an unbounded position normalized to 0…1; groups same-sign runs (gap ≤ 0.10 s); rejects runs < 0.08 s or < 8 net steps; emits `source: "controller"` events with signed direction, speed, confidence (0.7–0.95, never 1.0 merely for detection).
- Source-priority contract: controller (CC6) > DVS/timecode > camera; never merged. `withControllerMovementProvenance` retags the fusion's "video" → "controller" and adds "controller" to `detectionSources`. Camera stays available as a diagnostic/fallback.
- Verification: `ControllerPlatterDecoderTests` 7/7, `MovementTraceDiagnosticsTests` 20/20, `CaptureReliabilityPhase1CoreTests` 321/321, pipeline 47/47, Debug build + build-for-testing + Release build all succeed, `git diff --check` clean.
