## 2026-08-22 (iOS DVS + MIDI parity — Tasks 1/2/3/4/6: hardware route adapter + multichannel PCM routing)
- Root cause: the Task 1/2 route-observation logic lived ad hoc inside `AudioEngine`, had no dedicated bridge type, and always downmixed every input channel to mono before analysis — correct for a 1–2 channel mic/line-in, but wrong for a multichannel USB interface (e.g. RANE ONE MKII), where blending all channels together would mix unrelated deck/mic signals into one incoherent mono stream. There was also no rule for which stereo pair to treat as selected: `selectedStereoPair` was always `nil` in practice.
- Files changed: `ScratchLab/Audio/iOSAudioHardwareRouteAdapter.swift` (new); `ScratchLab/Models/AudioHardwareRouteState.swift`; `ScratchLab/Audio/AudioEngine.swift`; `ScratchLabDesktopTests/AudioHardwareRouteStateTests.swift`; `ScratchLab.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` (new file added to the iOS `ScratchLab` target only — it is not part of `ScratchLabDesktop` or `ScratchLabWatch`); plus `TASKS.md` and this log.
- Task 1 (adapter): extracted the AVAudioSession→`AudioHardwareRouteState` bridge out of `AudioEngine` into `iOSAudioHardwareRouteAdapter`, an `@MainActor` `ObservableObject` publishing `routeState`. It owns hardware observation (`refresh(session:inputNode:isInputActive:signalLevel:)`), PCM-activity updates (`updateActivity`), and manual pair selection (`selectStereoPair`, unused by UI yet — no UI work was in scope). `AudioEngine` now delegates to it instead of the former private `IOSAudioHardwareRouteObserver` struct, with no change to `AudioEngine`'s own published `audioHardwareRouteState` shape or timing.
- Task 3 (selection rules): added `AudioHardwareRouteState.StereoPair.resolveSelection(availablePairs:remembered:)` — pure, Foundation-only, testable on macOS — implementing "remembered pair if still available, else first available pair, else nil" with no possible crash on empty/malformed input. The adapter remembers the confirmed pair per device UID across `refresh()` calls, so a device that drops out and reconnects restores the previous choice instead of resetting.
- Task 2 (multichannel PCM): added `AudioHardwareRouteState.StereoPair.extractInterleaved(_:channelCount:)` (pure, testable) and `AudioEngine.extractStereoPair(from:pair:)` (handles both interleaved and non-interleaved `AVAudioPCMBuffer` layouts) so the buffer is read for exactly the selected pair's two channel indices before any downmixing. `processAudioBuffer`/`audioPacket(from:selectedStereoPair:)` now extract-then-average that pair to mono for the existing (unchanged) analysis pipeline; when no pair is selected (a genuine single-channel mic) it falls back to the prior full-downmix behavior byte-for-byte, so mic/line-in output is unchanged. A 14-channel RANE-style buffer selecting pair "3/4" now reads hardware indices 2/3 only, rather than averaging all 14 channels together as it did before this change.
- Task 4 (diagnostics): DEBUG-only logging moved into the adapter, firing only when device/transport/sample-rate/channel-topology/selected-pair actually change (never per callback), formatted as the requested "Audio Route Changed" block with Device/Transport/Sample Rate/Channels/Stereo Pairs/Selected fields.
- Task 6 (tests): added default-first-pair, remembered-pair-restored, remembered-pair-fallback, and invalid/mono-metadata-returns-nil-safely cases for `resolveSelection`, plus interleaved-extraction correctness (including the RANE "pair 3/4 → indices 2/3" example from spec) and two malformed-buffer-returns-nil-safely cases for `extractInterleaved`. All 18 tests (10 prior + 8 new) passed on the macOS test host. `AudioEngine.extractStereoPair`'s `AVAudioPCMBuffer`-based glue has no automated coverage — this project has no iOS-hosted XCTest target (`ScratchLabDesktopTests` is macOS-only, `TEST_HOST` = the macOS app), so buffer-level extraction can only be exercised by running the app.
- Verification: `plutil -lint` and `git diff --check` passed. macOS Debug build succeeded; focused `AudioHardwareRouteStateTests` passed 18/18 on the macOS test host; iPhone 17, iPad (A16), and Apple Watch Series 11 (42mm) simulator Debug builds all succeeded with code signing disabled, zero warnings in touched files.
- Remaining limitations (explicit, per phase scope): no live DVS validation was performed; no timecode source was connected; no MIDI implementation exists yet; no turntable/control-vinyl hardware is available so RANE ONE MKII naming/UID/channel topology/sample rate remain unconfirmed until a real USB-C connection is observed; no UI changes were made (device-picker UI for `selectStereoPair` does not exist yet). Nothing was committed.

## 2026-08-22 (iOS MIDI Phase 2 — CoreMIDI transport; uncommitted)
- Starting state: `main` at `06fc8c0`. Four pre-existing working-tree modifications (`ScratchLab/Audio/AudioEngine.swift`, `ScratchLab/DesignSystem/ScratchLabDesignSystem.swift`, `ScratchLab/Views/PracticeModeView.swift`, and `ScratchLabDesktopTests/DVSControlVinylAnalyzerTests.swift`) were preserved and not edited during this MIDI phase.
- Root cause: iOS already compiled the shared controller profiles, learned mappings, registry, parsing, and verification models, but had no CoreMIDI client/input port. The safe channel-message framing implementation was also private to `MacCaptureEngine`, preventing iOS from reusing its malformed-packet, SysEx, and realtime-byte handling.
- Files changed for this phase: `ScratchLab/Models/ControllerInput/MIDIChannelMessageParser.swift` (new); `ScratchLab/Models/ControllerInput/MIDIReadinessState.swift` (new); `ScratchLab/MIDI/iOSMIDIManager.swift` (new); `ScratchLab/ScratchLabApp.swift`; `ScratchLabDesktop/Services/MacCaptureEngine.swift`; `ScratchLabDesktopTests/MIDIPacketBoundsCrashFixTests.swift`; `ScratchLab.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj`; plus `TASKS.md` and this log.
- Architecture: the pure shared parser frames complete MIDI 1.0 channel-voice messages, ignores realtime bytes without disturbing framing, skips SysEx/System Common safely, rejects running status and malformed/truncated data, and converts only the existing registry-supported Note On/Off, CC, and Pitch Bend types into `ParsedMIDIMessage`. `MacCaptureEngine` now calls the shared type with its packet-list extraction and all downstream dispatch unchanged.
- iOS transport: `IOSMIDIManager` uses `MIDIClientCreate`, `MIDIInputPortCreate`, `MIDIGetNumberOfSources`, `MIDIGetSource`, `MIDIPortConnectSource`, matching disconnect/dispose cleanup, and CoreMIDI notifications for source refresh. It connects discovered sources, traverses live `MIDIPacketList` storage using the same safe field-offset approach as macOS, and publishes source identity, latest parsed message, count, and readiness. `RootContainerView` owns it as a `StateObject` and exposes it through the environment; no visible UI or controller action was added.
- Truth/logging: `MIDIReadinessState` is unavailable with no source, deviceConnected from connection evidence alone, and receivingMessages only after a valid supported packet. DEBUG device logs are emitted once per discovered source and message logs are throttled to one per second. Release adds no logs.
- Tests: existing packet-list traversal, multiple-packet, oversized-packet, packet-boundary, SysEx, realtime, malformed-input, two-byte-message, and left/right-channel tests remain green; added shared-model conversion and readiness truth tests. `MIDIPacketBoundsCrashFixTests` passed 15/15 in each of two configured runs.
- Verification: iPhone 17 simulator Debug build succeeded; the built app installed and launched without MIDI sources (PID returned by `simctl`); macOS Debug build succeeded; `plutil -lint` and `git diff --check` passed. The retained App Intents metadata notice is unrelated. DVS code and `AudioEngine.swift` were not edited in this phase.
- Hardware status: MIDI transport is implemented but NOT VERIFIED on physical USB MIDI hardware. DVS remains NOT VERIFIED by this phase; no DVS path changed.

## 2026-08-23 (V3.2 Phase 9 watchOS + iOS Watch-hub design-system adoption; uncommitted)

- Root cause: `ScratchLabWatch/WatchCaptureView.swift` (the entire watchOS UI) and `ScratchLab/Views/WatchCaptureHubView.swift` (the iOS Watch-capture hub) still built every color from literal `Color.red`/`.cyan`/`.white.opacity()`/`Color(hex:)`/manual gradients, and — more significantly — the Watch screen's richest state signal, `WatchMotionRecorder.transferStatus` (a free-text status line covering everything from "Sent to your paired device." to "Couldn't send to your paired device. Will retry automatically." to "Pair your watch with your device to send sessions.") had zero color coding at all, despite the task's explicit scope naming "warning, failed, disconnected states" and "progress and completion presentation."
- Files changed: `ScratchLabWatch/WatchCaptureView.swift`, `ScratchLab/Views/WatchCaptureHubView.swift`, `ScratchLab/DesignSystem/ScratchLabDesignSystem.swift`, `ScratchLab/DesignSystem/ScratchLabCoreColors.swift` (new), `ScratchLab.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj`; plus `TASKS.md` and this log. Every pre-existing dirty file was preserved.
- Cross-target design-system strategy (the phase's central decision, made before any view edit): confirmed via `project.pbxproj` that `ScratchLabDesignSystem.swift` compiles only into `ScratchLab` (iOS) and `ScratchLabDesktop` (macOS) — two `PBXBuildFile` entries, not three. Checked *why* before assuming it could just be added: its "Platform color mapping" section calls `Color(uiColor: .secondarySystemBackground)` and `Color(uiColor: .systemBackground)` under `#if canImport(UIKit)` — both true `canImport` on watchOS, but neither system-color role exists in watchOS's UIKit subset, so adding the file wholesale would fail to compile on the Watch target, not just be architecturally heavy-handed. Rather than force the full 2,200+ line iOS/macOS file (materials, `StatusBadge`/`Chip`/card/button component families sized for phone and desktop) onto a Watch target that shouldn't have any of that, extracted only the platform-safe primitive genuinely needed — pure RGB math, no UIKit/AppKit — into a new file: `ScratchLab/DesignSystem/ScratchLabCoreColors.swift`, containing the `Color(scratchLabHex:)` initializer (relocated from `ScratchLabDesignSystem.swift`, which no longer declares it) and a 12-constant `ScratchLabCoreColor` enum (`accent`/`success`/`warning`/`danger`/`info`/`textPrimary`/`textSecondary`/`textTertiary`/`canvas`/`raised`/`controlFill`). This file was added to all three targets (`ScratchLab`, `ScratchLabDesktop`, `ScratchLabWatch`) in `project.pbxproj`, following the exact precedent the project already establishes for `WatchMotionCapture.swift`/`CaptureReliability.swift` (small pure-Swift files already shared across the iOS and Watch targets): one `PBXFileReference`, one group-child entry, three `PBXBuildFile` entries (one per target's own `Sources` build phase). `ScratchLabDesignSystem.swift`'s `Sem.accent/success/warning/danger/info/textPrimary/textSecondary/textTertiary` and `Surface.canvas/raised` now read `ScratchLabCoreColor.*` instead of re-declaring the same hex literal a second time, so every overlapping role has exactly one canonical value across all three targets — not two independently-maintained palettes that could silently drift apart. The `pbxproj` diff is narrow and strictly additive: no existing `PBXBuildFile`/`PBXFileReference`/group/build-phase entry was altered or removed, only new ones added.
- Implementation — `WatchCaptureView.swift`: root background moved from a literal `Color.black`/`Color.blue.opacity(0.45)` gradient to the same canvas→raised→canvas gradient shape used at every other root-background site in the app (via `ScratchLabCoreColor.canvas`/`.raised`). The "Ready"/"Recording" status label moved from cyan/red to `.success`/`.danger` — a genuine readiness/recording state, kept semantically distinct from the Start/Stop button's own `.accent`/`.danger` (the button's color is "primary action," the label's color is "current state," and they happen to agree on Recording=red but intentionally disagree on Ready=green vs. the button's Start=accent-cyan). The Connection/Transfer info rows — previously plain, uncolored text — now use `.info` when paired/reachable and `.textTertiary` when not, matching "connected but not ready: informational" and "searching or waiting: neutral" exactly (the Transfer row's "Searching" value is the literal case the rule names). Added `WatchTransferStatusTone`, a private, purely-presentational classifier over `transferStatus`'s existing, unmodified string values — it changes no string, adds no state, and any string it doesn't recognize (e.g. a future wording change) falls back to neutral rather than guessing a color: `"Ready"`→success, `"Recording"`/`"Motion capture is unavailable on this watch."`/`"Unable to save the motion session."`→danger, `"Sent to your paired device."`→success, `"Queued the motion session for device import."`→info, and the remaining eight setup/retry/recoverable-issue strings (e.g. `"Pair your watch with your device to send sessions."`, `"Couldn't send to your paired device. Will retry automatically."`)→warning, since none of them is a hard failure and all are self-recovering or need a one-time setup step — matching "actionable attention: warning," not failure red, for exactly the case the task calls out ("do not use failure red for ordinary coaching correction when warning amber is truthful").
- Implementation — `WatchCaptureHubView.swift` (full `ScratchLabDesign` access — this file is iOS-target only): header/workflow/sessions cards moved onto `Typo.pageTitle/.pageSubtitle/.cardHeading/.body` and `.scratchLabCard(.selected/.standard)`; the "Paired Watch"/"Watch App Installed"/"Reachable Right Now" status rows (previously all identically colored regardless of true/false) now use `Sem.info` for "Yes" and `Sem.textTertiary` for "No" — informational, deliberately never `Sem.success`, since being paired/installed/reachable is a connection fact, not proof the watch is ready to capture; the free-text "Import Status" row stays neutral `Sem.textSecondary`. `WatchCaptureSessionCard`'s date/motion-count text and its "Share JSON"/"Share CSV" export badges moved off literal hex fills onto `Sem.accent`/`Sem.success` fill with `Sem.textOnAccent` label text, matching the exact dark-on-bright-fill convention every other primary/success control in the app already uses.
- Behavior preserved: no `WatchConnectivity` message name/payload, command routing, session synchronization, capture start/stop/pause/resume/cancel, connectivity evaluation, background delivery, activation state, haptic, timer, session metadata, persistence, complication, feature-flag, bundle-identifier, capability, or entitlement changed. `WatchMotionRecorder.swift`/`WatchMotionCaptureStore.swift` (the actual connectivity/capture services) were not touched — only their already-published, unchanged `@Published` values are read for display. No unsupported command, dead control, fake live state, or optimistic connectivity claim was added; the transfer-status tone classifier strictly recolors strings the model already produces, never invents one. Two new accessibility labels were added (the Start/Stop button, the Ready/Recording status text) specifically to satisfy "recording must remain visually unmistakable and must not rely on colour alone" — additive, not a change to the two pre-existing accessibility labels on the instructional text and footer note, which are untouched.

Compiling ... WatchCaptureView.swift ... ScratchLabCoreColors.swift ... (in target 'ScratchLabWatch')`, confirming a genuine watchOS compile of the edited sources. Generic iOS Simulator Debug build succeeded (this also rebuilds and embeds a fresh `ScratchLabWatch.app`). macOS Debug build succeeded. `plutil -lint` on `project.pbxproj` passed. `git diff --check` passed. `ScratchLabDesignTokensTests` (22 tests) passed 22/22 in isolation, confirming the `Sem`/`Surface` hex-constant relocation onto `ScratchLabCoreColor` changed no actual resolved color value. `scripts/build.sh all` passed 47/47 capture-pipeline fixtures and reproduced the Phase 8 baseline exactly on the first run — **2,982 tests / 47 skipped / 100 failures, exit 65** — with the full failing-test-name set (57 unique names) diffed against the Phase 8 log and confirmed byte-identical. ## 2026-08-29 (Capture-integrity Slice A: shared capture-evidence model; uncommitted)

- Selected task: the first slice of the capture-integrity batch Karl approved after the physical iPhone take-002 evidence (screen recording plus two Review/HUD screenshots) showed live blue notation responding while the capture HUD read `MOTION Motion Missing`, and Review simultaneously rendered `Ready to keep`, `Motion pending`, `Motion Missing`, and `Fader: No movement`. The full ten-requirement prompt was classified as roughly eight architectural slices and decomposed before any edit; Karl selected Slice A and directed that the AHHH/Serato requirement become an explicit new mode (Slice G) rather than a deletion, so the gate recorded in `AI_HANDOFF/next_prompt.md` is superseded rather than silently overwritten.
- Root cause (verified by reading, not inferred): motion presence was derived solely from a linked Apple Watch artifact at three independent sites — `ScratchLab/Views/CompanionCameraView.swift` `handleFinishedRecording` (`watchMotionCaptureStore.hasLinkedCapture(...)`), the `makeSessionExportPackage` take builder in the same file (`linkedWatchCapture != nil`), and `ScratchLab/Services/SessionExportCoordinator.swift`'s recovery builder (`motionPresent: linkedWatchCapture != nil`). The take's genuine controller evidence was already produced by `iOSMIDIManager.detectedNotationSnapshot()` and persisted into the sidecar via `broadcaster.persistingDetectedNotation(...)` four lines above the first of those checks, then ignored by all three. A valid RANE platter take with no Watch paired therefore reported motion missing in Review and exported as motionless.
- Second, larger root cause found while implementing: export validation would have actively rejected the newly-truthful takes. `packageValidationIssues` appended "claims watch motion, but no linked watch artifact was supplied" whenever `motionPresent == true` without a watch session, and the canonical-context builder hard-`throw`s `SessionExportError.invalidSessionMetadata` on the same condition. Fixing presence without fixing these two gates would have converted a mislabeled-but-exportable take into an unexportable one.
- Files changed: `ScratchLab/Models/CaptureCore.swift`, `ScratchLab/Views/CompanionCameraView.swift`, `ScratchLab/Services/SessionExportCoordinator.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktopTests/CaptureReliabilityPhase1Tests.swift`, plus `TASKS.md`, `AI_HANDOFF.md`, `AI_HANDOFF/next_prompt.md`, and this log. All four source/test files were already pre-existing dirty; every unrelated dirty file and hunk was preserved. No `project.pbxproj` edit was needed because every touched file already has target membership and the tests were appended to an existing test file. No resource, Info.plist, entitlement, signing, or Copy Bundle Resources change.
- Implementation: added a domain-only `CaptureMotionEvidence` to `CaptureCore` — `CapturePlatterMotionEvidence` (`absent` / `steadyRotationOnly(forwardRuns:)` / `gesture(movementRuns:reversalRuns:)`), a fader event count, `CaptureWatchMotionEvidence`, and `CaptureDVSMotionEvidence` — with `CaptureMotionEvidenceResolver` as the single place that turns persisted take evidence into it. Per Karl's adjustment the type carries no user-facing strings; presentation is deferred to Slice B so the two platforms cannot drift into different vocabularies for one state.
- Gesture-vs-motor discrimination is structural, not a new threshold: a released powered platter emits forward-only CC6 runs, and every real scratch contains a pull-back, so the discriminator is the presence of a decoded backward run. This reuses `derivePlatterMovementEvents`' existing noise gates (`minRunDuration` 0.08 s, `minRunSteps` 8) instead of introducing a second independently-tunable layer. A typed `ScratchMovementKind.isReversal` was added rather than string-matching `direction`.
- Per Karl's adjustments: fader events never establish motion presence (a cut is recorded evidence but is not platter movement, so a fader-only take has no gesture to review); DVS reports `.unsupported` and is excluded from `motionSources` because `CompanionCameraView` has no timecode-pipeline feed at take finalization today — modelled for exhaustive switching, never fabricated; and both the live export builder and the recovery builder resolve from the same persisted `sidecar.detectedNotation`, so a live-exported take and the same take rebuilt from disk resolve identically.
- Export validation was made source-aware via `SessionExportTake.motionSources`, an additive optional field with two derived predicates (`claimsWatchBackedMotion`, `claimsMotionWithoutAnySource`). `nil` sources preserve the historical Watch-only behaviour exactly, so pre-existing callers and fixtures validate as before; `[]` with `motionPresent == true` is now explicitly a contradiction rather than being silently treated as a Watch claim; and a watch artifact belonging to a different session or take is still rejected on both the controller-backed and watch-backed paths. `SessionExportTake` is an in-memory `Sendable` input struct, not a serialized type, and `take_log.csv` / `session_manifest.json` carry no motion column, so there is no on-disk export-schema change.
- `markReviewMotionPresent()` was renamed to `markReviewWatchMotionLinked()` and now records the Watch as a source on the existing evidence instead of flipping a bare boolean, so a late-linking Watch cannot erase platter evidence a take already had.

First, the operator message was a hardcoded `"Ready to keep"` string literal decided independently at two call sites in `CompanionCameraView.swift` — `handleRecordingFinished` and `applyAudioPresence` — neither of which consulted motion at all. Second, `GuidedCaptureReviewStateResolver.motionAssessment` computed `syncStatus` and `motionStatusTitle` as two independent strings over the same inputs, and deliberately returned `"Motion pending"` for the same `motionPresent == false` that produced `"Motion Missing"`. Third, `CaptureReview` stored all four labels as separately-settable `var`s, so even a correct resolver could be partially applied.
- Files changed: `ScratchLab/Models/CaptureCore.swift`, `ScratchLab/Views/CompanionCameraView.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktopTests/CaptureReliabilityPhase1Tests.swift`, plus `TASKS.md`, `AI_HANDOFF.md`, `AI_HANDOFF/next_prompt.md`, and this log. - Implementation: replaced `GuidedCaptureMotionAssessment` with `GuidedCaptureReviewState`, built from two typed enums — `CaptureReviewReadiness` (`recordingInterrupted` / `takeTooShort` / `missingAudio` / `calibrationInvalid` / `retakeRecommended` / `readyToKeep`, ordered most- to least-blocking, exactly one reported) and `CaptureMotionStatus` (`present` / `optional` / `missing`), plus a `CaptureMotionRequirement` that names why motion is or is not required. `GuidedCaptureReviewStateResolver.reviewState(...)` now also takes `recordingFailed` and `duration`, which is what removes the call-site decision that let a hardcoded literal survive next to a missing-motion pill. The 1.0-second floor moved out of two duplicated call sites into `minimumKeepableTakeDuration`.
- `CaptureReview`'s `syncStatus`, `motionStatusTitle`, `motionPresent`, and `operatorMessage` became computed projections of a single stored `reviewState`, so they cannot be set independently or partially refreshed. `syncStatus` is deliberately a projection rather than an independent string: when motion is the blocker it now returns `motionStatus.title` verbatim, so the sync and motion labels can restate each other but can never contradict each other. `applyAudioPresence` and `markReviewWatchMotionLinked` both collapsed onto one private `resolvedReviewState(...)` helper, replacing two hand-maintained copies of the same branch ladder.

These replaced the single standalone Fader block in both `landscapeDetails` and `decisionColumn`. `steadyRotationOnly` is named separately from `absent` so a running motor does not read as a capture failure. DVS is deliberately omitted: a permanent `Unavailable` row would imply a source the product does not have, and it returns when a real feed exists. `reviewStatusPills` now switches on the typed readiness instead of comparing `syncStatus` against the string literal `"Ready"`.

Two of the new tests are exhaustive over all seven resolver inputs and assert that no combination can yield `"Motion pending"` or pair `readyToKeep` with `motionStatus == .missing`. The pre-existing `testGuidedCaptureReviewStateDoesNotInventWatchMotionWhenMotionIsSkipped` was migrated to the new API and still asserts the same behaviour.   1. The earlier Slice C stub said the `"Raw ch 15 · CC 8"` Hardware Setup row "shows as configured while persisting zero events". That was false — `mappingDescription` already returned `"Not active · expected Raw ch 15 · CC 8"`. The claim was written without reading the function and is retracted.

Slice C must not be described as the fix for that screenshot.
- Real defects fixed. (a) `MIDIActionResolver` resolved transport against `MIDIHardwareRegistry` but resolved crossfader ONLY from a learned mapping, even though the registry already carries a `.certified` RANE crossfader binding (`absoluteCC(number: 8)`, `channel: 15`). Startup auto-applies the verified mapping, but `selectMIDISource` in `CompanionCameraView` and `MainMenuView` does not, so a device selected manually recorded no fader evidence at all. (b) Nothing bounded the END of the take window: `resetCapturedPlatterEvents()` set the start bound at real recording start, but events accumulated until the next take's reset, so controller moves made between Stop and movie finalization — precisely the window the finalization watchdog exists for — were decoded into the finished take.

No `project.pbxproj` edit: every touched file already has target membership and all tests were appended to an existing test file.
- Implementation: added `FaderMappingSource` (`learned` / `certifiedRegistry`) and put it on `MIDIResolvedAction.crossfader`. A new resolution step 2b sits after the learned mapping and before the pad router, gated on three conditions so it can never become a blind "any CC8 is a crossfader" sniff — the registry must produce a real match for the device identity, that match must be `.certified` (not `.verified`/`.unverified`), and a non-diagnostic `.crossfader` binding must match the message via the existing shared `MIDIControlBinding.matches(_:)` rather than a second comparison. Learned mappings still win unconditionally, including when learned onto a non-default address.
- Per Karl's decision A, the registry path is EVIDENCE-ONLY: `playbackEngine.setCrossfaderPosition(...)` is now called only when `source == .learned`, so recognising a crossfader from the registry never starts cutting ScratchLab's audio on a device the user never mapped. Normalization was split accordingly — a learned control keeps its own min/max/inverted calibration, while a certified binding uses the plain 7-bit `MIDIControlNormalization.sevenBit`, never another action's calibration borrowed by accident.
- Provenance is persisted on `CaptureCore.RawMixerMIDIEvent.mappingSource` as an Optional, so Swift's synthesised decoder tolerates its absence and sidecars written before provenance existed decode as `nil` = "unknown provenance", never "learned". It is read back by `CaptureMotionEvidenceResolver.faderMappingSource(from:)` off the persisted mixer events, so a recovered take reports the same source the live take did, and flows into `CaptureMotionEvidence.faderMappingSource`, the review Fader row (`4 events · learned` / `· certified default`), and `SessionExportTake.faderMappingSource`. As with Slice A's `motionSources`, `SessionExportTake` is an in-memory input struct, so there is no on-disk export-schema change.
- The take-end bound is `markCaptureStopped()`, called from `stopTake()` before finalization begins, recording a monotonic take-relative stop instant in the same `CACurrentMediaTime()` domain as `captureBaselineTimestamp` — deliberately not reconciled against the sidecar's wall-clock `startedAt`/`endedAt`. The filter itself lives in shared `CaptureMotionEvidenceResolver.eventsWithinTakeWindow(_:stopRelativeTime:)` rather than staying dispatcher-private, because `iOSMIDIManager.swift` is an iOS-target-only file and is therefore unreachable from the macOS test target; making the boundary a shared rule is both better design and the only way to test it. The stop instant itself is inside the take (`<=`).
- No fabrication: `deriveDetectedNotationFaderEvents` and its `minimumValueDelta` / `minimumCutDelta` gates are completely untouched. Two tests pin this — a held-open fader emitting 20 identical values still yields zero events under certified provenance, and a genuine fast full-travel cut still registers.
- macOS mapping unification is deliberately OUT of scope per Karl's decision B and is documented as a KNOWN PLATFORM DIVERGENCE in `MIDIActionResolver.swift`: macOS keeps its own `CrossfaderCCMapping` in `UserDefaults` (`MacCaptureEngine`), predating the shared learned-mapping model and not registry-aware, so a certified registry crossfader default applies on iOS only and macOS still requires an explicit crossfader learn.

## 2026-08-29 (RANE right-deck playback routing: measured 10-channel fix, physically approved; uncommitted)

- Selected task: Karl's physical report that ScratchLab's AHHH was driven by the right platter and right upfader and reached master output, but the RANE's LEFT channel meter LEDs illuminated. Started from commit `37e2d1d1`; no commit was amended or reset.
- Investigation discipline: the first pass STOPPED without editing rather than guessing a pair. The official RANE ONE MKII User Guide v1.1 was downloaded and searched in full — it documents the Deck Source switch ("Set this switch to the desired audio source from this channel: USB A or B ... or Line", and "The meter next to this knob indicates the signal's volume level") but contains NO USB channel numbering whatsoever, so the right-deck pair was not provable from official documentation. Project history offered only two negatives (13/14 lit the wrong deck; 3/4 now lit the left meter) and no positive identification. A DEBUG requested-versus-granted diagnostic was deployed instead, and Karl separately confirmed from hardware that USB output 1/2 is the left deck and 3/4 is the right deck.
- ROOT CAUSE, measured on device rather than inferred: the RANE ONE MKII exposes **10** USB output channels. `IOScratchPlaybackEngine` hardcoded `raneOutputChannelCount = 14` and gated the whole channel-map path on `session.maximumOutputNumberOfChannels >= 14`. `10 >= 14` is false, so `preferredHardwareChannelCount` collapsed to 2, `outputPairStartIndex` became nil, and `channelMap` was never assigned — playback fell through to the device's first output pair, 1/2, the LEFT deck. The diagnostic captured every step: `requestedChannels=2 supportsRaneOutputPairPreRequest=false / grantedChannels=10 maximumChannels=10 / outputNodeChannels=10 / channelMap=[nil] count=0`, identical at `after-configure` and `after-engine-start`.
- The pair index was CORRECT throughout. `raneOutputPairStartIndex = 2` (destination 2/3 = physical 3/4 = right deck) was never the operative value, which is why both the earlier 13/14 assumption and the later 3/4 value produced a wrong-deck meter — neither was ever applied. The old DEBUG log printed `preferredHardwareChannelCount`, i.e. the value ScratchLab REQUESTED, so it read `hardwareChannels=14` even when the map was never installed; that single flaw is what hid the defect across two previous attempts.
- `AVAudioSession` was explicitly CLEARED as a suspect and not modified. It granted 10 of 10 channels on request, and `options=8` decodes to `.defaultToSpeaker` alone, which did not block multichannel USB output. No category, mode, or option change was made — the earlier hypothesis that `.defaultToSpeaker`/`.mixWithOthers` were forcing stereo was disproved by the measurement.
- Files changed: `ScratchLab/Models/DVSHardwareProfile.swift`, `ScratchLab/Audio/iOS/IOScratchPlaybackEngine.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktopTests/CaptureReliabilityPhase1Tests.swift`, plus `TASKS.md`, `AI_HANDOFF.md`, `AI_HANDOFF/next_prompt.md`, and this log. No `project.pbxproj` change: the routing policy was deliberately placed in `DVSHardwareProfile.swift`, which is already a member of BOTH the iOS and macOS targets and is Foundation-only, so the pure policy is unit-testable from the macOS test target even though the engine that applies it is an iOS-target-only file. It also puts the DVS input pair and the playback output pair side by side with their namespace independence documented in one place.
- Implementation: `RanePlaybackRoutingPolicy` with `rightDeckPairStartIndex = 2` and `minimumRequiredOutputChannels` DERIVED as `rightDeckPairStartIndex + 2 = 4`, never a guessed device size. `decide(portName:grantedOutputChannels:outputNodeChannels:)` returns `.raneRightDeck(channelMap:)`, `.ordinaryStereo`, or `.unroutable(RoutingFailure)`. The engine now requests the connected route's actual `maximumOutputNumberOfChannels`, reads back the granted `outputNumberOfChannels` AND the output node's own channel count (the session granting enough is not proof the node did), builds the map sized to the real destination count, applies it, then READS IT BACK and verifies `mapPlacesRendererOnRightDeck` before permitting playback.
- Fails loudly instead of silently: a recognized RANE route that cannot reach the right deck now throws `IOScratchPlaybackRoutingError.raneRightDeckUnavailable` and does not start AHHH at all, rather than degrading to ordinary stereo. That silent fallback WAS the bug — plain stereo lands on 1/2, the left deck, with nothing to indicate anything was wrong. Non-RANE routes keep the ordinary stereo graph byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Test debt repaid: `testRaneScratchPlaybackUsesRightDeckOutputThreeFourIndependentlyOfDVSInput` asserted the literal source string `"let raneOutputPairStartIndex = 2"`. It passed for the entire duration of this bug, because the constant it pinned was never wrong. Replaced with 17 behavioural tests in a new `RanePlaybackRoutingPolicyTests` suite: 10-output accepted (the measured shape), 4-output accepted (the derived minimum), 14-output still works (the old guess must not become an implicit requirement), fewer than four rejected rather than routed to 1/2, output-node shortfall rejected even when the session grants enough, renderer mapped only to destination 2/3, left pair explicitly silenced, master pair 13/14 never targeted, read-back verification rejecting left-deck/swapped/nil/short maps, non-RANE routes including a multichannel non-RANE interface remaining ordinary stereo, DVS input 3/4 unchanged and independent, and right-upfader × right-deck-crossfader gain ownership unchanged.
- DVS input remains physical 3/4 in the independent Core Audio input namespace. Both input and output legitimately use 3/4; the policy documents that this is not a collision and that neither value may be derived from the other.
- PHYSICAL ACCEPTANCE (Karl, iPhone K + RANE ONE MKII): AHHH plays through the right deck, only the right channel meter responds, right upfader and right-deck crossfader control it, master output is normal, DVS unaffected. The on-device log corroborates the ears exactly: `[RANE-ROUTING] stage=configured route=Rane ONE MKII rane=true granted=10 max=10 outputNode=10 map=[-1,-1,0,1,-1,-1,-1,-1,-1,-1] onRightDeck=true decision=raneRightDeck`, and the identical map at `stage=after-engine-start running=true`, proving the assignment survives engine startup.
- Verification: `RanePlaybackRoutingPolicyTests` 17/17 twice. Regressions: `MIDIUserMixerGainTests` 39/39, `MIDIFaderCurveTests` 22/22, `DVSControlVinylAnalyzerTests` 40/40, `MIDIPlatterContinuousDriveTests` 17/17, `CrossfaderMappingProvenanceTests` 21/21, `CaptureMotionEvidenceTests` 13/13, `GuidedCaptureReviewStateTests` 10/10. Isolated iOS Simulator build, signed device build, and macOS `build-for-testing` all succeeded. Fixtures 47/47. `git diff --check` clean. `scripts/build.sh all` exit 65, 3090 tests / 49 skipped / 11 failures — the failing-name set diffed IDENTICAL to the post-restore baseline (9 names), with the test count up by exactly 17.
- Investigated and cleared, not hidden: `PlatterTestSampleLoadTests` reported 5 failures ("not found: dvs_ahhh") when run STANDALONE via `xcrun xctest`, but passes inside the full plan; the `dvs_ahhh` resource is present in both the source tree and the built bundle, and this slice's diff touches nothing near `ScratchSampleResolver` or any resource. Same shared-state/isolation fragility already recorded for `MIDILearnEngineTests` (3 failures standalone, passing in-plan). Unrelated to routing; a test-isolation cleanup slice is now clearly warranted.
- Remaining risk: only the RANE ONE profile is recognized, so every other output route behaves exactly as before. If a future RANE route ever grants fewer than four channels, AHHH will now refuse to play with a truthful message rather than sneak onto the left deck — intended, but a visible failure mode where there was previously a silent one. The meaning of RANE output pairs beyond 1/2 and 3/4 remains undocumented by the manufacturer; this slice needs only the two Karl confirmed. Nothing committed or pushed.

It is pure and clock-free — `apply(_:at:)` is given the instant — and returns an ordered `[CaptureFinalizationEffect]` the caller performs. `CaptureFinalizationBudget` (12s first wait, 3s retry, 5s audio inspection) makes `worstCaseSaving` an explicit 15s. `CaptureFinalizationDeadlineScheduler` is the only place a deadline becomes elapsed time, and scheduling replaces the previous timer, so a second watchdog has nowhere to come from. `CaptureFinalizationClock` injects the time source.

## 2026-08-30 (Capture-integrity Slice F: iOS "inconsistent metadata" export failure fixed; still physically unapproved)

- Trigger: the first real iPhone export of a freshly kept take failed with "This session has inconsistent metadata." The prior Slice F record claimed a green gate; that record was honest about the tests but did not cover this path, because every fixture used a whole-second `createdAt`. The earlier "COMPLETE" entry must not be read as a physical result.
- Root cause: `SessionArchiveBuilder.validateStagedPackage` wrote `manifests/session_metadata.json`, `export_metadata.json`, `session_review.json`, and `session_replay.json` through the canonical `JSONEncoder` whose `.iso8601` strategy serializes **whole seconds**, then decoded those files back and compared the decoded documents against the in-memory ones (`metadata == expectedMetadata`, `exportMetadata == …`, `review == …`). A `Date` with a sub-second component can never survive that round trip, so a byte-identical, fully valid export was rejected as inconsistent metadata. Measured directly: `Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_710_000_000.372)` encodes to `"2024-03-09T16:00:00Z"` and decodes back 0.372 s earlier, while re-encoding the same value is byte-stable.
- Why only freshly kept takes: a guided kept session's `createdAt` is a live `Date()` and the kept-session ledger persists it with the default (`.deferredToDate`) strategy, so the fraction survives in memory and across a reload. `packageForLocalRecordingSession` instead derives `createdAt` from sidecar dates that have already been through `.iso8601`, so recovered sessions are always whole-second. That is exactly why device recovery exports succeeded while the freshly kept take did not.
- Fix: compare the staged BYTES against the same documents re-encoded through the same canonical encoder — the pattern `session_manifest.json` and every notation document already used in the same function. Decoded documents are retained only for the structural identity assertions (session ID, take IDs, counts, replay/review generatedAt agreement). `createdAt` is not rounded or mutated, no take is filtered out, no default is fabricated, and no `try?`/`compactMap` was introduced. The check is strictly stronger than before: it now also proves each staged file is the canonical byte-for-byte serialization, not merely an equal-valued one.
- Also added, because "This session has inconsistent metadata." named nothing an operator or a device log could act on: `SessionExportValidationReason` and `SessionExportValidationFailure`. A staged-package rejection now carries the specific check that fired alongside the unchanged `SessionExportError`. The reason vocabulary is closed and contains check names only — never file paths, performer names, notes, or capture content — and the coordinator surfaces it through the existing `validationReport`, so the coarse error, its user message, and retry/cancel semantics are unchanged.
- The fail-closed check "take claims `.platter` motion but its notation recorded no movement events" was deliberately preserved and now reports by name. That path is still unreproduced on hardware and is covered by a deterministic named-error regression rather than being relaxed.
- Files changed: `ScratchLab/Services/SessionExportCoordinator.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktopTests/CaptureReliabilityPhase1Tests.swift`, `TASKS.md`, `AI_HANDOFF.md`, `AI_HANDOFF/next_prompt.md`, and this log. `ScratchLab/Models/CaptureCore.swift` and `ScratchLab/Views/CompanionCameraView.swift` were left at their existing Slice F state. Protected `project.pbxproj`, `ScratchLab.xcscheme`, `Info.plist`, and the untracked `CalibrationCameraOverlayTests.swift.plist` were not altered or staged.
- Tests added (7, all in `CaptureReliabilityPhase1CoreTests`): sub-second-`createdAt` export success; sub-second preservation plus canonical-bytes assertion (fails if anyone "fixes" this again by flooring `createdAt`); single kept take exported exactly once; restored two-take ledger exported with both takes exactly once; coordinator share path plus cancellation for a sub-second session; platter-motion-without-movement named-error regression; coordinator named-reason reporting with staged captures preserved across the failure.
- Regression proof, not assumed: the fix was temporarily reverted to the value comparison, the target rebuilt, and the four sub-second cases confirmed to FAIL; the fix was then restored and they passed. Without that step the new tests would not be evidence of anything.
- Verification: focused set 14/14 in two executions. Affected regressions green — `CaptureRecoveryPhase2CoreTests` 58/58, `ScratchLabNotationAndExportTests` 29/29, `SessionExportRoundTripTests` 1/1, `SessionReviewMetadataTests` 17/17, `SessionQualityAnalyzerTests` 15/15, `SessionReplayTimelineTests` 7/7, `SessionReplayDocumentTests` 8/8 (135 total, 0 failures). Isolated generic iOS Simulator and macOS Debug builds succeeded; capture fixtures 47/47; `git diff --check` clean. ## 2026-09-04 - Anchor the routine take boundary on confirmed media start; fix export levels, durations, dates, and the canonical validator

- Selected task: audit and fix capture/export against the real archive `session_2026_09_04_h_baby_scratch_95_bpm` (49 MB, one take, `f8a91511-9452-4951-895a-bfd198425b4e`).
- This entry replaces a draft appended earlier in the same uncommitted session. That draft was written before the final verification run and described three policies that were subsequently changed after review: a -1 dBFS mix ceiling that attenuated the captured scratch, a session date derived from the exporting machine's current time zone, and a fixture "re-export" whose manifest and date were patched by hand rather than produced by the app. Nothing was committed at any point; the numbers below are from the final tree only.

### What the fixture actually showed

- Traced timing from the fixture's own evidence, not from its manifest. `debug/take-1_movement_trace.json` gives `recordingStartHostTime = 405047.2542529168` and `finalizationHostTime = 405071.36508108344` (span 24.1108 s); `debug/take-1_raw_platter_debug.json` gives `endTime = 24.11985762498807`. Camera presentation times run to `405067.50092` (epoch + 20.2467 s) and the movie is 19.36895 s, so the writer took about 0.88 s from `startRecording(to:)` to its first written sample, and finalization (onboard-audio mux + sidecar write) consumed the remaining ~3.87 s.
- Correction to the reported hypothesis: there was no timed-stop countdown in the macOS recorder at all. The only duration bound was `movieOutput.maxRecordedDuration`, hardcoded to `RoutineCaptureDefaults.defaultTakeLengthSeconds` (64 s), so the requested length was never enforced and the take ended when the operator stopped it.
- Root cause of the "24 second" label: `SessionArchiveBuilder.preparePackage` derived each take's `duration` from `sidecar.endedAt - sidecar.startedAt`. That wall-clock span includes writer startup before the first media sample and mux/finalization after the last one, and both timestamps persist at whole-second ISO-8601 precision, which is why the 24.1198 s span serialised as exactly `24`. It was never a measurement of playable media.
- Root cause of the timing offset: movement, platter, and MIDI epochs were stamped just before `movieOutput.startRecording(to:)`, roughly 0.88 s ahead of the media.

### Capture side

- `RoutineDetectedNotationBuilder.startedAt`, `platterRecordingStartTime`, and `movementTraceRecordingStartHostTime` are left unarmed at request time and rebased in `didStartRecordingTo` onto one confirmed media-start epoch. `RoutineTakeTimeline.takeRelativeTime` drops any instant before it instead of clamping to zero, and `RoutineDetectedNotationBuilder.rebaseEpoch(to:)` discards pre-roll strokes.
- `maxRecordedDuration` now follows `RoutineCaptureDefaults.requestedTakeLengthSeconds(for:)`. It is measured in recorded media time, so startup cannot be charged against it. A wall-clock backstop is armed only from the confirmed media start.
- `didFinishRecordingTo` is the single close for MIDI, movement, platter, and the onboard audio tap.

### Planned versus actual duration

- Added `CaptureSessionConfig.plannedTakeDurationSeconds` (the request, never overwritten) and `SessionExportMetadata.plannedTakeDurationSeconds`. `totalDurationSeconds` is now the measured playable duration read from the captured audio, with the wall-clock span kept only as a fallback for an unreadable artifact.
- Backward compatibility: `plannedTakeDurationSeconds` decodes faithfully (absent stays absent) and the legacy fallback to `takeDurationSeconds` lives in `requestedTakeLengthSeconds(for:)`, at the point of use. An earlier attempt migrated on decode and was reverted: it made a decoded config unequal to the config it was written from, which broke `GuidedCaptureKeptSessionStore`'s idempotency check and caused `testGuidedKeptLedgerSingleTakeReloadIsDurableAndIdempotent` to fail (the ledger was rewritten with a 10 s later `updatedAt`, same byte count, different bytes). Decoding must not mutate data.
- The legacy field was overloaded (export also wrote the measured aggregate into it), so for legacy data the two meanings genuinely cannot be told apart. Honouring the stored value is the documented choice, re-validated against the take-length range. Every capture through the current UI stamps `plannedTakeDurationSeconds` explicitly, so the fallback only applies to pre-existing records.

### Generated audio levels

- The export summed beat voices with no headroom (`beat_only` peaked at 1.218279, +1.714933 dBFS, 480 samples at or above full scale) and the mix hard clamped with `max(-1, min(1, ...))` (50 samples pinned to exactly +/-1.0).
- Added `ScratchLabBeatEngine.GeneratedAudioHeadroom`: one attenuate-only linear gain, never a per-sample clamp. Generated stems are held to -1 dBFS.
- The captured recording is never turned down to make room for generated audio. In `mixScratchWithTiming` the scratch runs at unity and headroom is found by lowering only the timing stem: the largest gain no greater than the nominal 0.55 for which `|scratch + gain * timing| <= ceiling` holds at every frame, solved exactly in one pass. The mix ceiling is -0.1 dBFS rather than -1 dBFS precisely because the fixture's captured scratch peaks at -0.234 dBFS and a -1 dBFS ceiling would have forced a ~0.77 dB attenuation of the recording. Only if the scratch alone exceeds the ceiling is the whole mix attenuated, and the applied `mixGain` is returned so that case is visible.

### Session date and time zone

- Documented in `docs/capture_spec_v1.md`. A session's date is the capture device's local calendar date at session start, used identically by the folder name, `session_manifest.json` `date`, and every take `date`; absolute instants stay UTC ISO-8601.
- The zone is persisted, not inferred: `CaptureSessionConfig.sessionTimeZoneIdentifier` is stamped when the session identity is created and is what export reads. Deriving from the exporting machine's zone would re-date a session exported after travel or a DST change.
- A legacy session with no recorded zone is dated in UTC. That fallback is deliberate and deterministic: such a session carries no evidence of where it was captured, so the only defensible date is a reproducible one, and UTC also matches what pre-policy exports already wrote for the manifest.
- `CaptureCanonicalFormatting.sessionDateString` was UTC while `archiveFolderName` used an unconfigured local `DateFormatter`, which produced the `2026_09_04` / `2026-09-03` split. Both now go through one helper pair.

### Canonical validator

- `probe_audio_metadata` no longer uses stdlib `wave` (which rejects WAVE_FORMAT_IEEE_FLOAT). It prefers ffprobe and falls back to a new RIFF chunk walker handling format tags 1/3/0xFFFE, JUNK/FLLR padding, and odd-size alignment.
- Take-log media paths resolve as written relative to the session root; `raw/` is tried only for a bare filename with no directory component, the legacy staging convention.
- Slate/clap warnings are gated on the manifest `*_required` flags on the take-log side as well as the manifest side.
- Added generated-stem peak enforcement and a folder/manifest/take date-consistency check.

### Files changed

`ScratchLab/Models/CaptureCore.swift`, `ScratchLab/Models/CaptureReliability.swift`, `ScratchLab/Services/ScratchLabBeatEngine.swift`, `ScratchLab/Services/SessionExportCoordinator.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktop/Services/MacCaptureEngine.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktop/Views/MacAnalyzerView.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktopTests/CaptureReliabilityPhase1Tests.swift`, `scripts/capture_pipeline_common.py`, `scripts/validate_session.py`, `scripts/test_capture_pipeline.py`, `scripts/fixtures/capture_pipeline/ffprobe_stub.py`, `docs/capture_spec_v1.md`, `TASKS.md`, `DEV_LOG.md`. `ScratchLab/Services/ClickTrackEngine.swift` and `ScratchLabDesktopTests/SessionReplayDocumentTests.swift` were already dirty before this task and were not touched.

XCTest plan `** TEST SUCCEEDED **`: both configured runs executed **3,258 tests, 51 skipped, 0 failures (0 unexpected)**, 270.99 s and 270.70 s. iOS, macOS, and watchOS builds each `** BUILD SUCCEEDED **`.

## 2026-09-04 - Separate the routine take safety cap from an operator-selected duration; record an explicit stop reason

- Selected task: resolve the metadata ambiguity in `session_2026_09_04_kk_baby_scratch_95_bpm`, which reported `plannedTakeDurationSeconds = 64` for a take whose media is 16.70 s. Exporter work from the previous entry was not revisited; that archive already validates and its canonical media/evidence is aligned.
- Verdict on the take: **manual stop**. Audio and all three stems are 16.70 s (736,470 frames at 44,100 Hz), video is 16.76863 s, camera observations stop at 16.7483 s, and the capture lifecycle span is 19.9037 s (`recordingStartHostTime 411305.21642675`, `finalizationHostTime 411325.12011633`), so the ~3.15 s tail is finalization. The 64 s bound was never approached.
- Origin of 64, traced: `RoutineCaptureDefaults.defaultTakeLengthSeconds = 64` (`CaptureCore.swift`, from commit `9fbbd65c` "Set default routine take length to 64 seconds"). It reached `plannedTakeDurationSeconds` through two sites added in the previous slice — `MacAnalyzerView.resolvedCaptureConfigForRecording()` and the `CaptureSessionConfig.routineCapture(...)` default argument. The macOS Capture panel has no take-duration control: it renders that constant as static text in two places, so the operator never selected it. It was always a safety cap feeding `movieOutput.maxRecordedDuration`, mislabelled as an intent.
- Renamed the constant to `defaultMaximumTakeDurationSeconds` and its label to `maximumTakeDurationLabel` ("Max 64 seconds"), and split the accessor in two: `plannedTakeDurationSeconds(for:)` returns the operator's explicit choice or `nil` with no fallback, and `maximumTakeDurationSeconds(for:)` resolves the effective bound (plan, then stored cap, then legacy `takeDurationSeconds`, then the default).
- Added `CaptureSessionConfig.maximumTakeDurationSeconds`. `routineCapture(...)` now defaults the plan to `nil` and the cap to 64. Legacy configs decode faithfully — absent stays absent — and their overloaded `takeDurationSeconds` is resolved at the point of use as the cap, never as a plan.
- Added `CaptureStopReason` (`manual`, `planned_duration_reached`, `interrupted`, `capture_error`, `media_limit`) and `LocalRecordingSidecar.stopReason`. `MacCaptureEngine` records the reason at the stop call site (`stopRoutineRecording(reason:)`, defaulting to `.manual`); the wall-clock backstop reports `plannedDurationReached` only when a plan exists and `mediaLimit` otherwise; `resolvedRoutineStopReason` lets AVFoundation's `AVError.maximumDurationReached` outrank the app's note, since that path bypasses `stopRoutineRecording`. Absent means "not recorded", never an inferred manual stop.
- Export: `SessionExportMetadata` gains `maximumTakeDurationSeconds` and reports `plannedTakeDurationSeconds` only for a validated explicit plan. `SessionExportTakeCaptureMetadata` gains `stopReason`, `plannedTakeDurationSeconds`, `maximumTakeDurationSeconds`, and `actualTakeDurationSeconds`. `totalDurationSeconds` is unchanged and still the measured playable duration.
- Validator: `validate_take_stop_reasons` reads the optional `manifests/session_metadata.json` and compares planned against actual **only** when `stopReason == planned_duration_reached`. A cap-bounded manual stop no longer looks like a shortfall; an unknown reason is an error; a missing reason warns; a plan that did not elapse warns.
- Watch and fader evidence untouched. The kk take exports `watch_source = none` and `faderEvents: 0`, and nothing was synthesised.
- Files changed: `ScratchLab/Models/CaptureCore.swift`, `ScratchLab/Services/SessionExportCoordinator.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktop/Services/MacCaptureEngine.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktop/Views/MacAnalyzerView.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktopTests/CaptureReliabilityPhase1Tests.swift`, `scripts/validate_session.py`, `scripts/test_capture_pipeline.py`, `docs/capture_spec_v1.md`, `DEV_LOG.md`.
- Also fixed a latent flake introduced in the previous slice: `testDecodingALegacyConfigDoesNotChangeItsValue` compared re-encoded bytes from two separate `JSONEncoder` instances. Foundation does not guarantee a stable key order between instances, so the comparison failed intermittently with an identical byte count and reordered keys. The first full gate of this slice failed on it (exit 65, 3,272 tests / 4 failures). Both round-trip assertions now go through one `assertEncodingIsStableUnderDecoding` helper using a fixed instant and `.sortedKeys`, and passed six consecutive focused runs. The same gate also surfaced `testMIDILearnStateTransitionsToListening` failing in one configuration and passing in the other — a pre-existing shared-state flake in the MIDI learn tests, untouched by this slice and left as-is.
- Focused results: `RoutineTakeDurationSemanticsTests` 12, `SessionExportDurationMetadataTests` 3, `RoutineTakeBoundaryTests` 6, `CaptureConfigMigrationTests` 9 — 30 executed, 0 failures, twice. `python3 scripts/test_capture_pipeline.py` 66/66 OK (58 before; eight new stop-reason gate tests). The gated `FixtureArchiveReExportTests` run through `preparePackage` + `createArchive` reports `stopReason=manual planned=24.0 maximum=64.0 actual=19.2` and the resulting archive validates PASS.
- Physical hardware verification remains unchecked in `TASKS.md`.

The Watch was already recording under an earlier command when the take asked for a new one.

Not stage 6: `resolveLinkedWatchCaptureArtifact` opens with `guard let fileName = sidecar.linkedMotionFileName else { return nil }` (`SessionExportCoordinator.swift:5625`), so with that field absent the exporter correctly reported `none`. ## 2026-09-04 - Mac Stop must end the Watch capture it started (BVB regression)

- Selected task: the Watch stop defect proven by `session_2026_09_04_bvb_baby_scratch_95_bpm`. That export is clean by every existing check - `stopReason: manual`, 19.4 s of audio, 19.235624 s of camera, all three stems at exactly 855,540 frames, `watch_source: watch`, the Watch CSV present and linked, canonical validator PASS - while the Watch CSV runs 0.0 to 37.8943409166659 s. The Watch recorded 18.4943409166659 s past the end of the take and the operator stopped it by hand. The previous artifact-association/write-back fix is working and was not touched: the motion reached the Mac, was linked, and exported.
- Root cause, in three parts, all in the Mac's stop path:
  1. **Ownership.** The Watch stop lived in `MacAnalyzerView.handleRoutineRecordingButton`, so only the Stop *button* ever sent one. Every other terminal path for a take sent nothing: the timed backstop in `scheduleRoutineTimedStop`, AVFoundation ending the take itself at `movieOutput.maxRecordedDuration` (which never calls `stopRoutineRecording` at all - see `resolvedRoutineStopReason`'s own comment), a capture error, a refused start, and a cancelled count-in.
  2. **Identity.** The button's call passed `sessionID: routineSessionSetup.config.sessionID` with `takeID: nil` - not the `TakeIdentity` the start was acknowledged under. The take ID was back-filled from `relayedWatchCaptureStore.activeTakeContext`, which is only populated when the start reply arrived acknowledged *and* matched a pending context.
  3. **No acknowledgement.** `CompanionCameraReceiver.requestWatchCaptureStop` returned `Void`. It reported only a local *send* failure; it never awaited the reply, never retried, never recorded an outcome. Anything downstream - iPhone relay not forwarding, Watch unreachable, Watch refusing - was invisible, and the take still exported as if the Watch had stopped on cue.
- Which of those three actually silenced this particular capture is not decidable from the archive, because nothing recorded it. That is itself the defect, and item 5 below is the fix for it.
- Fix, by layer:
  - `CaptureReliability.swift`: `CaptureWatchStopOutcome` (`notRequested`, `sent`, `unreachable`, `timedOut`, `identityRejected`, `stopped`, `failed`), `CaptureWatchMotionTransferState` (`notApplicable`, `pending`, `completed`), `CaptureWatchStopDiagnostics`, and `CaptureWatchStopPolicy` (2.0 s per acknowledgement attempt, 2 attempts, so a 4.0 s ceiling). `WatchCaptureControlReply` gains an **optional** `stopOutcome`, so a peer that predates it still decodes and `CaptureWatchStopPolicy.outcome(for:)` derives the fallback. `WatchCaptureCommandCoordinator`'s timeout is now command-aware instead of always saying "start".
  - `WatchMotionStopCommandResolver` (pure, shared, therefore testable off-device) is the Watch's decision table: idempotent on a repeated command or an idle recorder, identity-scoped, and honest about which branch it took.
  - `WatchMotionRecorder`: both `didReceiveMessage` overloads now run one `resolveControlCommand`, so the duplicated start/stop logic is gone. A stop naming a session or take the watch is not recording is **refused** and says why; a duplicate stop performs no second finalize; a handled stop still answers `syncState: notRequested` (the shipped contract `withWatchSync` depends on) and adds `stopOutcome`.
  - `MacCaptureEngine` now owns the stop. `applyPendingWatchReply` grants ownership only on an `acknowledged` start for a complete identity. `requestWatchStopIfNeeded(reason:)` dispatches exactly once per take, keyed `sessionID:takeID`, and is called from `stopRoutineRecording`, `finalizeRoutineRecording` (the backstop for AVFoundation's own end), `cancelPendingRoutineReservation`, and every abandoned-start path. It returns immediately; the handshake runs on a task and its outcome is merged into the take's sidecar on disk.
  - `CompanionCameraReceiver.requestWatchCaptureStop` is now `async` with acknowledgement, a bounded timeout, and a single retry on timeout only (unreachable/rejected/failed are answers, not silence). Start and stop share one `awaitWatchControlReply`.
  - `MacAnalyzerView` no longer sends its own stop; it installs the transport (`watchStopRequestHandler`) and nothing else.
- Media finalization is never blocked. The stop is dispatched asynchronously and bounded at 4.0 s total; `persistWatchStopDiagnostics` re-reads the on-disk sidecar and writes only the stop-diagnostics field, so the late-association merge (`mergingLatestWatchAssociation`) is preserved, not clobbered. Adopting a link upgrades `motionTransferState` to `completed` but never invents a stop record that was not requested.
- Export (additive, app-side; canonical `watch_source` stays two-valued and unoverloaded): `SessionExportTakeCaptureMetadata` gains `watchStopOutcome`, `watchStopDetail`, and `watchMotionTransferState`. `watchSyncState` keeps its existing meaning - the *start* handshake.
- Validator: `validate_take_watch_duration` compares the Watch CSV's largest `elapsed_time` against the take's canonical audio duration. Over 2.0 s of overrun warns; over 4.0 s errors, because that is longer than the stop handshake can honestly take. The raw CSV is read-only - the overrun is reported, never truncated away. Run against the real BVB archive this now reports: `95 BPM take 01: watch motion runs 37.894s against a 19.400s take - 18.494s past the end of the take (max 4.000s). The watch kept recording after the take ended.` Status FAIL, exit 1. The archive itself was not modified.
- Files changed: `ScratchLab/Models/CaptureReliability.swift`, `ScratchLab/Models/CaptureCore.swift`, `ScratchLab/Services/WatchMotionCaptureStore.swift`, `ScratchLab/Services/SessionExportCoordinator.swift`, `ScratchLabWatch/Services/WatchMotionRecorder.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktop/Services/CompanionCameraReceiver.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktop/Services/MacCaptureEngine.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktop/Views/MacAnalyzerView.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktopTests/CaptureReliabilityPhase1Tests.swift`, `scripts/validate_session.py`, `scripts/test_capture_pipeline.py`, `docs/capture_spec_v1.md`, `DEV_LOG.md`, `TASKS.md`.
- NOT proven on hardware. A fresh Mac + Watch capture and export is required: press Stop on the Mac only, and confirm the Watch stops on its own, the Watch CSV ends within 4.0 s of the take audio, `watchStopOutcome` reads `stopped`, and the validator passes.
- Gate result, `scripts/build.sh all`, one run: **exit 65**. Cause is a pre-existing flake, not this work. `scripts/test_capture_pipeline.py` passed 79/79. The macOS XCTest plan runs two configurations over the same 3304 tests: configuration 1 passed 3304/3304 with 51 skipped and 0 failures; configuration 2 failed on exactly one test, `TimecodeRealtimeIngressRingTests.testConcurrentSPSCStressAccountsForEveryAttempt` (`XCTAssertEqual failed: ("19264") is not equal to ("19268")`), which had passed in configuration 1 minutes earlier in the same run. It is a lock-free SPSC ring stress assertion in `TimecodeRealtimeIngressRing`, a file this slice does not touch (`git diff --name-only` lists nothing under the timecode path). Re-run standalone via `xcrun xctest` it passed 10/10. Not fixed here, and not claimed as passing: it is a real flaky test and deserves its own slice.
- Because `set -e` stopped `build.sh` at the test stage, the three platform builds it would have run next were run directly afterwards on the same tree: iOS `** BUILD SUCCEEDED **`, macOS `** BUILD SUCCEEDED **`, watchOS `** BUILD SUCCEEDED **`.
- New suites, all green in both configurations: `MacWatchStopDispatchTests` 8/8, `WatchMotionStopCommandResolverTests` 7/7, `CaptureWatchStopOutcomeTests` 7/7, `WatchStopDiagnosticsSidecarTests` 5/5. New validator regressions in `AppExportValidationTests`: 7, including the 18.494 s BVB overrun rejection, a bounded-finalization acceptance, the 4.0 s boundary, and a check that the raw Watch CSV is byte-identical after validation.

## 2026-09-04 - Hardware run 1 failed; ownership gate was fail-open

- First hardware run of the Watch-stop fix, session `4ee15cc0-0c26-4aa9-b7a1-d004e7c9b548` take-001, exported as `session_2026_09_04_nmnmnm_baby_scratch_95_bpm`. The Watch still did not stop when Stop was pressed on the Mac. Karl confirmed he pressed record on the Mac and the Watch app was open at the time.
- The diagnostics added earlier localised it in one read, which is what they were for. Export: `watchSyncState: failed`, `watchStopOutcome: notRequested`, `watchMotionTransferState: notApplicable`, `watchMotionExported: false`, no `watch/` CSV, `stopReason: manual`, 17.3 s take. Sidecar: `watchCommandID eac9f34a-2cfc-455d-8e73-6b14bc7dba5f`, `watchRequestedAt` and `watchAcknowledgedAt` both `03:27:02Z`, `watchStopDiagnostics: null`, one `watch_sync` audit event. Nothing new in `RelayedWatchCaptures` since 14:22, so no motion reached the Mac for this take.
- Root cause, and it is a defect in the previous fix rather than the transport: `applyPendingWatchReply` granted stop-ownership only on `reply.syncState == .acknowledged`. That is fail-open in the dangerous direction. A degraded *reply* is not evidence the Watch did not start - the command can reach the wrist and Core Motion can begin while the answer is lost, late, or an explicit failure. The Mac then owned nothing, dispatched no stop, and the take exported `notRequested` while the Watch kept recording until Karl stopped it.
- Fix: `CaptureWatchStopPolicy.startMayHaveLeftWatchRecording(_:)` states the fail-closed rule. `acknowledged`, `requested`, `failed` and `timedOut` all arm the stop; only `unavailable` (no peer, watch app absent or unreachable, motion unavailable) and `notRequested` own nothing, because those are the two states where the command demonstrably never reached a recorder. A stop for a capture that never started is harmless - the Watch's handler answers `alreadyStopped` and does no work. `resolvedWatchTakeIdentity(for:)` falls back to the reserved take identity when a synthesized failure carries an incomplete one.
- Second gap this exposed, also fixed: `withWatchSync` dropped the reply's `detail`, so `watchSyncState: failed` carried no recoverable reason and the first failure needed a second run to diagnose. The `watch_sync` audit event now records it.
- Still unknown and deliberately not guessed at: *why* the start handshake returned `failed`. The next run will record it in the `watch_sync` audit detail.
- Tests: `MacWatchStopDispatchTests` 10/10 (adds `testAFailedStartHandshakeStillOwnsAndStopsTheWatch`, `testATimedOutStartStillOwnsTheWatch`, `testAnUnavailableStartOwnsNothing`), `CaptureWatchStopOutcomeTests` 8/8, `WatchStopDiagnosticsSidecarTests` 6/6, `WatchMotionStopCommandResolverTests` 7/7, `RoutineFinalizationWatchMergeTests` 3/3, `WatchSyncStateExportTests` 2/2 - 36/36 green. macOS build-for-testing succeeded; macOS and iOS device builds succeeded and were installed to iPhone `K` and the paired Series 10 Watch.
