## 2026-09-04 - Watch stop confirmed working on hardware; validator was measuring the wrong quantity

- Second hardware run, session `1ce25396-2268-4583-918f-ed372bee7b2a` take-001, exported as `session_2026_09_04_kjhgt_baby_scratch_95_bpm`. **Karl confirmed the Watch stopped by itself.** The original defect is fixed.
- Timeline from the Watch's own record and the Mac sidecar, all UTC: start command 03:39:14; Watch acknowledged and began recording 03:39:15; Mac gave up on the start ack at 03:39:17 and recorded `failed`; media began 03:39:20; Stop pressed and the watch stop dispatched 03:39:30; **Watch ended 03:39:30**; finalization adopted the link at 03:39:33, superseding the stale `failed`; the stop resolved `timedOut` at 03:39:35. The Watch stopped in the same second it was asked. Overrun at the end is effectively zero. 1,549 samples, `estimatedDroppedSamples: 0`, clean 100 Hz to the last sample.
- The fail-closed ownership fix is visibly working: the start handshake returned `failed`, and the stop was dispatched anyway. Under the previous build that take would have recorded `notRequested` and the Watch would have run until stopped by hand.
- **My validator check was wrong and produced a false FAIL on a good take.** It computed `watch_duration - take_duration` and called the result "past the end of the take". Those are different questions: the Watch's window and the take's window do not share a start, because the Watch begins when the start handshake resolves while media begins after the count-in and camera startup. This take held 15.411 s of motion against a 10.000 s take, and the entire 5.411 s was a **lead-in**, not an overrun. The earlier BVB reading of "18.494 s past the end of the take" was stated with more confidence than the data supported; a count-in cannot account for 18.5 s so most of it was real overrun, but the exact figure was not knowable from that archive.
- Export gains four instants so the two are separately answerable: `takeStartedAt`, `takeStopRequestedAt` (the moment the stop was dispatched - the authoritative end of the media window), `watchCaptureStartedAt`, `watchCaptureEndedAt` (the Watch's own clock).
- `validate_take_watch_duration` now compares **ends**: overrun is `watchCaptureEndedAt - takeStopRequestedAt`, warning past 2.0 s and error past 4.0 s. Lead-in (`takeStartedAt - watchCaptureStartedAt`) is reported separately, warning past 3.0 s, because a long lead-in means the start handshake stalled rather than that anything overran. An archive with no alignment gets a warning naming the difference and saying plainly that a late stop cannot be told apart from an early start - it is never reported as an overrun. Re-run against the kjhgt export the status is PASS with the lead-in surfaced; with the real instants supplied it is PASS with no overrun line.
- Remaining defect, not addressed here and deliberately not guessed at: **the relay's reply path takes about 5 s in both directions.** The Watch acknowledged the start at 03:39:15 and it had not arrived by 03:39:17; it stopped at 03:39:30 and the ack had not arrived by 03:39:35. Both handshakes therefore time out even though the Watch acts immediately, which costs every take a spurious `failed`/`timedOut` and a needless ~3 s lead-in from the blocking start await. This is a latency problem in Mac -> iPhone -> Watch, not a stop-dispatch problem, and it needs its own slice.
- Tests: 82/82 capture-pipeline fixtures (rewritten around the alignment model, including the `1ce25396` lead-in case and the BVB overrun case). macOS suites 36/36. macOS and iOS device builds succeeded; all three targets reinstalled.
- Files changed: `ScratchLab/Services/SessionExportCoordinator.swift`, `scripts/validate_session.py`, `scripts/test_capture_pipeline.py`, `ScratchLabDesktopTests/CaptureReliabilityPhase1Tests.swift`, `docs/capture_spec_v1.md`, `DEV_LOG.md`, `TASKS.md`.
- Alignment export verified end-to-end (2026-09-04). Take `1ce25396-…` take-001 re-exported through the new build now carries `takeStartedAt: 2026-09-04T03:39:20Z`, `takeStopRequestedAt: 2026-09-04T03:39:30Z`, `watchCaptureStartedAt: 2026-09-04T03:39:15Z`, `watchCaptureEndedAt: 2026-09-04T03:39:30Z` - identical to the values derived by hand from the routine sidecar and the linked motion file before the fields existed, so the exporter is reading the right sources. `validate_session.py` reports **PASS**, exit 0, with one warning naming the 5.000 s lead-in and no overrun line. The same archive FAILED under the duration-based check. `watchStopOutcome` remains `timedOut`, correctly, because the acknowledgement genuinely did not arrive inside the bound - the degraded handshake is still reported rather than smoothed away by the corrected overrun measurement.
- Caveat: this was a re-export of the existing take, not a fresh capture. It proves the export and validator path; it does not add a second hardware confirmation of the stop itself.

## 2026-09-04 - Relay acknowledgement latency: two serializations removed from the reply path

- Symptom from session `1ce25396-…`: the Watch stopped in the same second it was asked (stop dispatched 03:39:30Z, Watch `endedAt` 03:39:30Z) yet the handshake still recorded `timedOut`, and the start ack likewise missed its 3 s bound although the Watch had acknowledged at 03:39:15Z. Forward fast, reply slow, in both directions.
- No timeout was widened. `CaptureWatchStopPolicy` is unchanged at 2.0 s per attempt, 2 attempts, and the validator's overrun thresholds are derived from it, so widening the bound would also have widened the check that catches a Watch which really did not stop.
- Two serializations were found on the **reply** path, both structural, neither on the forward path - which is why the command always arrived promptly while the acknowledgement did not:
  1. **Watch.** `resolveControlCommand` called `stopCapture()`, which stops Core Motion *and* builds the session, encodes it and writes it, before `makeReply` was reached. The relayed artifact for that take is 1.26 MB for 1,549 samples; `WatchMotionCaptureCodec.encoder.encode` plus an atomic write of that size runs on the main queue and sat directly on the acknowledgement path. Split into `beginStop()` (stops Core Motion, takes the samples, clears active state - everything an acknowledgement should wait for) and `finalizeStoppedCapture(_:)` (relay batches, session build, persist, `queueTransfer`). The relay stop path now calls `beginStop()`, replies, and schedules finalization on the next main-queue turn. `stopCapture()` is retained unchanged in behaviour for the watch-UI entry point. Idempotency is unaffected: `isRecording = false` still happens synchronously inside `beginStop()`.
  2. **iPhone.** `sendWatchControlStatus` dispatched onto `captureQueue`, which is also `videoOutput.setSampleBufferDelegate(self, queue:)` - so the Watch's acknowledgement queued behind every camera frame. Added a dedicated serial `controlQueue` and moved `sendWatchControlStatus`, `sendWatchAvailability` and `sendWatchRelayLifecycle` onto it. The forward command path was never affected because it runs on `DispatchQueue.main`, which is exactly why the evidence showed a fast forward leg and a slow return leg.
- Measurement added so the next run can attribute any residual latency instead of merely reporting `timedOut`: `CaptureWatchStopDiagnostics.watchHandledAt` records when the Watch handled the stop by its own clock, and `resolvedAt` is now always the Mac's own resolve instant rather than being dated from the reply. `watchHandledAt - requestedAt` is the forward leg and `resolvedAt - watchHandledAt` is the return leg. Both are exported as `watchStopHandledAt` and `watchStopResolvedAt`.
- NOT proven on hardware. The next take must show `watchStopOutcome: stopped` rather than `timedOut`, `watchSyncState: acknowledged`, and a lead-in below the 3.0 s warning. If it still times out, the two exported instants will say which direction to look at next.
- Tests: macOS watch suites 38/38 (adds `testTheStopAcknowledgementIsNotGatedBehindFileWorkOrCameraFrames`, which pins both serializations, and `testStopDiagnosticsCanAttributeLatencyToADirection`); capture-pipeline fixtures 82/82; macOS build-for-testing, macOS build, watchOS build and iOS device build all succeeded; all three targets reinstalled.
- Files changed: `ScratchLabWatch/Services/WatchMotionRecorder.swift`, `ScratchLab/Services/CompanionCameraBroadcaster.swift`, `ScratchLab/Models/CaptureReliability.swift`, `ScratchLab/Models/CaptureCore.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktop/Services/MacCaptureEngine.swift`, `ScratchLab/Services/SessionExportCoordinator.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktopTests/CaptureReliabilityPhase1Tests.swift`, `DEV_LOG.md`.

## 2026-09-04 - Real root cause of every timed-out handshake: the relay minted a new command ID

- Third hardware run, session `63d7b603-88f8-4565-9380-d4b5851dc549`, exported as `session_2026_09_04_hj_baby_scratch_95_bpm`. Start `failed`, stop `timedOut`, `watchStopHandledAt` absent, no linked motion, no `watch/` directory. The new per-leg instants proved the point they were added for: `watchHandledAt` nil means no reply was received **at all**, in either direction - so this was never latency.
- **Root cause.** `WatchMotionCaptureStore.requestRemoteCaptureStart` and `requestRemoteCaptureStop` both default `commandID` to a fresh `UUID()`. `ScratchLabApp.handleRemoteWatchControlCommand` called them without passing the Mac's command ID through. The watch therefore replied under an ID the Mac had never issued; `WatchCaptureCommandCoordinator.resolve` found nothing in `pendingCommands`, filed the reply in `finalizedReplies` and returned, and the awaiting continuation for the Mac's real command was never resumed. **Every start and every stop timed out, unconditionally, no matter how fast the watch answered.** Session `1ce25396-…` is the proof in the other direction: the watch stopped in the same second it was asked and the Mac still recorded `timedOut`.
- This also explains the earlier readings that looked like transport latency and were not: the "3 s start ack didn't arrive" and "4 s stop ack didn't arrive" were both this. The two serializations removed in the previous entry (watch replying only after writing a 1.26 MB file; the iPhone relaying acks on the camera's sample-buffer queue) are real and worth keeping, but they were not the cause. Recorded plainly because the previous entry framed them as the fix.
- Fixes:
  - `handleRemoteWatchControlCommand` forwards `commandID: payload.commandID` for both start and stop, so the reply the Mac awaits is the reply it gets.
  - Control commands are delivered by a direct `onWatchControlCommand` closure from `CompanionCameraBroadcaster`, installed in `configureWatchRelay()` alongside every sibling relay callback. The previous path went through `.onChange(of: pendingWatchControlCommand)` in the app's view body, so capture control depended on the SwiftUI update cycle. `pendingWatchControlCommand` is still published, for UI and debugging only.
  - `WatchCaptureCommandCoordinator` now records `orphanedReplyCommandIDs` - a reply nobody awaited is the exact shape of this defect, and it was previously silent.
- New diagnostic so this class of failure is self-reporting: the relay sends a `.requested` **receipt** the moment it has a command, before forwarding. `resolve` treats `.requested` as a receipt and deliberately does not finalize the await. `CaptureWatchStopDiagnostics.relayReceivedAt` and the export's `watchStopRelayReceivedAt` carry it. A timeout with no receipt means the phone never heard the command; a timeout with a receipt means the phone heard it and the watch did not answer. `timedOut` alone could not tell those apart, which is what made this take three round trips.
- Tests: macOS watch suites 41/41, adding `testAReplyUnderADifferentCommandIDNeverResolvesTheCommand` (pins the root cause), `testTheRelayCarriesTheMacsCommandIDThroughToTheWatch`, and `testARelayReceiptDoesNotFinalizeTheCommand`. Capture-pipeline fixtures 82/82. macOS build-for-testing, macOS build, generic iOS build and iOS device build all succeeded; all three targets reinstalled.
- NOT proven on hardware. The next take should show `watchSyncState: acknowledged`, `watchStopOutcome: stopped`, and a lead-in below the 3.0 s warning.
- Files changed: `ScratchLab/ScratchLabApp.swift`, `ScratchLab/Services/CompanionCameraBroadcaster.swift`, `ScratchLab/Models/CaptureReliability.swift`, `ScratchLab/Models/CaptureCore.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktop/Services/CompanionCameraReceiver.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktop/Services/MacCaptureEngine.swift`, `ScratchLab/Services/SessionExportCoordinator.swift`, `ScratchLabDesktopTests/CaptureReliabilityPhase1Tests.swift`, `DEV_LOG.md`.

## 2026-09-04 - App Store Connect Info.plist blockers fixed (approved by Karl)

Four `Info.plist` findings from the audit, applied with explicit approval. `SOUL.md` otherwise puts these files behind a separate ask. No build settings, entitlements, signing, bundle IDs, or `Copy Bundle Resources` were touched.

- **P0 - macOS build number was pinned to 20.** `ScratchLabDesktop/Info.plist` hardcoded `<string>20</string>` while `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION` is `21` for every app target, and `ScratchLab/Info.plist` and `ScratchLabWatch/Info.plist` both resolve `$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)`. iOS and macOS share `com.machelpnz.scratchlab`, so that is one ASC record shipping two different build numbers at marketing version 1.0.1 - and the macOS number had stopped tracking the project entirely, so every future bump would have left it behind. Now `$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)`.
- **P1 - the Core Audio process tap had no usage description.** `MacCaptureEngine.swift:5105-5116` builds a `CATapDescription` and calls `AudioHardwareCreateProcessTap` to capture the DJ app's output for Direct Capture. That is TCC-gated on macOS 14.4+, and the plist declared camera and microphone but no `NSAudioCaptureUsageDescription`, so the permission could not be granted. Added, worded to `PROFILE.md`'s App Store safety rules - it states what is recorded and that audio stays on the Mac unless the user exports it, and claims nothing about analysis.
- **P2 - the watch declared 11 icon files it does not ship.** `CFBundleIconFiles` (twice, top level and inside `CFBundlePrimaryIcon`) listed `AppIcon24x24@2x` through `AppIcon1024x1024`. The asset catalog's real filenames are `watch-appLauncher-38mm@2x` and friends, and the built bundle contains no such PNGs - only a compiled `Assets.car`. Both stale arrays removed; the icon resolves through `CFBundleIconName: AppIcon` plus `ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME`, which is the correct mechanism and is unchanged.
- **P3 - invalid key.** `ScratchLab/Info.plist` carried `LSApplicationCategory` alongside the real `LSApplicationCategoryType`. The former is not a key the system reads. Removed.

- All three plists pass `plutil -lint`. Four regressions added so none of these can silently revert: `testAllPlatformsShipTheSameBuildNumber`, `testMacDeclaresAUsageDescriptionForTheAudioProcessTap` (conditioned on the tap still existing in the source, so it cannot outlive the feature), `testWatchDoesNotDeclareIconFilesItDoesNotShip`, `testIOSDoesNotDeclareTheInvalidApplicationCategoryKey`.
- Deliberately NOT done: `ScratchLabWatch` still has no `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`. Adding one needs a new file reference and a `Copy Bundle Resources` entry in `project.pbxproj`, which is a separate approval. It is also not currently a blocker - no required-reason API is used anywhere in `ScratchLabWatch/` (no `UserDefaults`/`@AppStorage`, no file-timestamp, disk-space or boot-time calls), so there is nothing it would have to declare today.
- Build and test verification deferred: Karl is mid hardware capture, and rebuilding would contend for CPU with a real-time take. To be verified on the next build.

No assertion was weakened and no existing test was touched.

## 2026-09-05 - TTM Prompt 1 committed: tear-capable canonical notation semantics

### Scope

Worktree `/Users/karlwatson/Downloads/ScratchLab-TTM`, branch `feature/ttm-tear-notation-alignment`, parent `3316fe0` (the verified Prompt 0 baseline; the hard CaptureCore calibration prerequisite is `579ace6`). Exactly two files changed, purely additive: 785 insertions to `ScratchLab/Models/CaptureCore.swift` and 746 to `ScratchLabDesktopTests/ScratchNotationCanonicalModelTests.swift`, 1,531 total with zero deletions, delivered as two single append-only hunks. Because no existing line was touched, no existing behaviour, resource or test could be altered.

The canonical types were extended rather than forked. `ScratchNotationDirection`, `ScratchNotationFaderState`, `ScratchFaderEventKind`, `ScratchMovementKind`, `ScratchNotation` and `ScratchNotation.BeatPattern` all keep their existing shapes and Codable payloads; the new layer sits beside them and bridges into them.

### What was defined

- `ScratchNotationMotionState`: forward, backward, stationary, released, unknown. `ScratchNotationDirection` keeps meaning travel polarity only and lifts losslessly. `.released` reports `travelDirection == nil` and `isStationary == false`, so free playback is motion and can never be counted as a hold. `ScratchMovementKind.motionState` is the single bridge from the capture vocabulary.
- `ScratchNotationFaderClickKind` with `init?(faderEventKind:)` returning nil for `.open`/`.closed`, so sustained state cannot be coerced into a click.
- `ScratchNotationEvidenceSource` and `ScratchNotationEvidence` (source, confidence, required reason, optional raw sample count). Capability is a property of the source: `platterTimeline` and `watchMotion` report `canEstablishFaderState == false`, `crossfaderRaw` reports `canEstablishPlatterMotion == false`, and `unknown` establishes neither.
- `ScratchNotationMotionLabel`: derived plus optional correction. The correction wins, the derivation survives, and the evidence record is never rewritten.
- `ScratchNotationCorrelatedState`: sounding, hold, ghost, ghostHold, releasedSounding, releasedMuted, unknown.
- Nested under `ScratchNotation`: `BeatSpan`, `PlatterMotionSegment`, `FaderInterval`, `FaderClick`, `PlatterGesture`, and the tempo-free beat-authored `GesturePattern` with a pure `validationIssues()`. Plus `BeatPattern.gesturePattern()` and `ScratchNotation.babyScratchGesturePattern`.

### Invariants established

- Platter and fader are independent streams synchronized only by the beat axis. `validationIssues()` contains no cross-stream rule by design.
- A tear is one same-direction gesture containing one or more bounded stationary intervals. N internal tear holds produce N+1 subdivisions by construction, not by assertion: each confirmed hold closes exactly one subdivision and one final subdivision is appended.
- A direction reversal is not a tear hold. Opposite-direction travel terminates the gesture, and `reversalBeats` names instantaneous turnarounds separately.
- A click is not a tear hold. Clicks exist only in `faderClicks`, and a motion segment must be a bounded interval, so no instant can enter the platter stream.
- A zero-velocity platter interval never creates a phantom click. The guard is structural: a click backed by platter provenance fails validation, so platter evidence has no path to minting fader evidence.
- Hold (stationary/open), ghost (travelling/closed) and ghost-hold (stationary/closed) are distinct, alongside sounding, releasedSounding and releasedMuted.
- Missing evidence remains unknown. An uncovered instant yields `faderState(atBeat:) == nil` and correlates to `.unknown`, never to implicitly open or closed - the same authority rule `ScratchNotation.faderEvents` already states.
- The platter stream is contiguous and total from beat 0, so an unobserved region must be stated as `.unknown` rather than left as a silent gap. Fader gaps are legal and mean unknown; abutting fader intervals may not repeat a state.
- Decoding stays tolerant and strictness lives in `validationIssues()`, matching the existing `ScratchNotation` doctrine. A decoded confidence of 7.5 survives decoding and is reported by validation.

### Baby Scratch preserved

`babyScratchGesturePattern` is forward, turnaround, backward with the fader open throughout: motion states `[.forward, .backward]` over `[0, 0.5]` and `[0.5, 1.0]`, a single coalesced open interval `[0, 1.0]`, no clicks, `reversalBeats == [0.5]`, two gestures each with zero tear holds and one subdivision, `.sounding` at both quarter points, and `durationBeats == 1.0`. A separate test proves the lift is non-destructive: `ScratchNotation.babyScratchCycle` compares equal before and after.

`build-for-testing` for `ScratchLabDesktop` on macOS succeeded. `test-without-building` over the six new suites - `TearMotionVocabularyTests`, `TearEvidenceAndLabelTests`, `TearGestureDerivationTests`, `TearStreamCorrelationTests`, `TearPatternValidationTests`, `BabyScratchTearCompatibilityTests` - ran 46 tests in 6 suites, all passed, zero failures and zero skips. The existing canonical regression set - `BabyScratchCycleTests`, `ScratchNotationTimingAuthorityTests`, `ScratchNotationLegacyRegressionTests`, `CanonicalTechniqueRegistryTests`, `CanonicalPlayheadTests`, `RegistryDrivenComparisonSurfaceTests`, `ScratchNotationFaderEventTests` - ran 57 tests in 7 suites and passed in both configurations, 114 executions, zero failures. `xcodebuild -scheme ScratchLab -destination generic/platform=iOS build` succeeded.

Affected platform builds only. The Watch target is genuinely unaffected: `CaptureCore.swift` is a member of the `ScratchLabDesktop` and `ScratchLab` sources phases and is not a member of `ScratchLabWatch`, so watchOS was not rebuilt. One serial `scripts/build.sh all` remains deferred to the end of the TTM batch, per the multi-boundary pacing rule.

## 2026-09-05 - TTM Prompt 2: lossless canonical gesture data model (uncommitted)

### Selected task and checkpoint

The explicit user instruction selected Prompt 2 only, overriding the unrelated first unchecked backlog task and the default full-build workflow. Before editing, the working directory was verified as `/Users/karlwatson/Downloads/ScratchLab-TTM`, branch `feature/ttm-tear-notation-alignment`, HEAD `57398919d508d1b94c206510aac12efed83a6478`, with a clean worktree and index. The HEAD commit contains Prompt 1 canonical semantics. No other worktree was accessed.

### Root cause and implementation

Prompt 1 supplies beat-domain semantics and derived gestures but no identity-bearing Codable record for measured/authored curve geometry and capture timing. This slice adds `ScratchNotation.GestureRecord` under the existing canonical model plus the separate `ScratchNotationProvenance` vocabulary. It adds no app consumer or alternate renderer/detector path.

- One stable producer-supplied gesture ID and direction; stable subdivision/hold/fader IDs survive decoding and timing edits. Existing IDs are never regenerated from timing.
- One explicit timebase per record: seconds from recording origin, or beats from authored-pattern origin. Curves, holds and fader data use that same axis. Coordinate space explicitly names signed sample position (fraction of source sample duration from cue, without clamping) or signed unwrapped platter displacement in revolutions.
- Ordered subdivisions retain arbitrary measured and target sampled curves independently, including their endpoints, irregular timing, negative coordinates and overshoot. No curve-family buckets, resampling, fitting or speed classification.
- Stationary holds must be bounded by exactly the surrounding same-direction subdivisions. The effective Prompt 1 motion label respects corrections while retaining derivation and raw evidence. N holds require N+1 motion subdivisions; `tear2` is derived from two pauses and three motion slices, never stored as truth. Releases, unknown states, travel labels, missing/zero-width/unbounded holds cannot assert a tear.
- Ratio convention chosen explicitly for this slice: relative MOVING-duration weights, excluding holds. Optional authored weights attach to subdivision IDs. The measured ratio is derived without rounding from measured seconds-domain boundaries; inferred, corrected, authored or unknown boundaries do not claim a measured ratio. Persisted raw durations retain the complete measurement.
- Independent fader edges and bounded open/closed observations retain their own source/provenance. Only bounded intervals establish sustained fader state; gaps and edges alone remain unknown. Derived interval correlation reuses `ScratchNotationCorrelatedState`, preserving hold/ghost/ghost-hold distinctions. Audibility is a mechanical classification, not proof of non-silent PCM. No platter observation creates a fader edge.
- Provenance distinguishes authored, measured, inferred, manually corrected and unknown independently of observation source/confidence/reason/raw sample count. Sensor capabilities remain those from Prompt 1. Authored sources cannot claim measured timing.
- Codable retains malformed evidence verbatim and `validationIssues()` reports it. Valid arrays are chronological, with stable ID tie-breaking for simultaneous fader edges; malformed order is retained and reported, not silently sorted. Derived labels, ratios and classifications are not serialized as competing truth.

## 2026-09-05 - TTM Prompt 3: calibrated platter-motion segmenter

### Selected task and root cause

The explicit user request selects exactly the pure segmenter slice over the unrelated first unchecked backlog item. Baseline: clean worktree and index at `0521b1e` (`feat(notation): add lossless canonical tear gesture records`) on `feature/ttm-tear-notation-alignment`, in `/Users/karlwatson/Downloads/ScratchLab-TTM`. No other working tree was accessed.

The existing canonical model describes gestures but has no calibrated evidence segmenter. `PlatterPositionTimeline` explicitly stores uncalibrated tracker units; the debug raw-lane adapter splits on every sign change without jitter thresholds. Neither is a safe implicit source of physical tear evidence. This slice adds a separate pure analysis entry point without wiring either existing path.

### Files and implementation

- `ScratchLab/Models/CaptureCore.swift`: additive `PlatterMotionSegmenter` (327 lines), beside the canonical model already included in iOS and desktop targets. Reuses the canonical seconds-span, curve-point, coordinate-space and direction types. No project membership change or Watch consumer.
- `ScratchLabDesktopTests/ScratchNotationCanonicalModelTests.swift`: 362 additive lines, 23 tests in two new suites, fixture generator and calibration helper. Existing tests unchanged.
- `TASKS.md`, `DEV_LOG.md`, `AI_HANDOFF.md`, `AI_HANDOFF/next_prompt.md`: slice status and verification only.

The input requires timestamped positions, sample confidence, an explicit calibration reference, physical-displacement or sample-position basis, origin, positive scale, forward sign, and configuration. Raw motor phase is rejected even if a scale is supplied. Calibrated positions remain signed and unbounded: no extrema normalization, modulo, clamp, implicit origin selection, timestamp sorting or interpolation. The caller must supply continuous physical/sample-position evidence; a basis tag does not prove calibration or turn a cached/event-driven trace into regularly observed position.

Consecutive sample pairs supply average speed. Two speed thresholds retain the prior compatible state inside the hysteresis band; ambiguous initial/sign-inconsistent motion is unknown. Minimum moving/hold durations qualify sustained runs. Excess stationary excursion or a stationary run containing hysteresis-band drift cannot establish a tear hold.

A jitter repair needs sustained matching neighbors, duration at most the repair limit, and bounded full position excursion. The repair limit must be strictly shorter than both minimum moving and hold durations. A short low-rate gap can join only sustained same-direction travel with consistent plausible average speed and valid input confidence. Missing stationary evidence is never bridged into a hold. Other gaps coalesce as unknown, break gestures and lower adjacent gesture confidence. Every repair retains original calibrated points, carries reasons and low confidence, and suppresses a measured ratio. Unsupported short intervals above the repair budget stay unknown rather than disappearing.

Output contains ordered total motion spans for valid clocks, calibrated points, same-direction gesture candidates, N bounded internal tear holds and N+1 moving subdivisions, opposite-direction reversal intervals, moving-duration fractions excluding holds, and explicit confidence/reasons. A stop between opposite directions is a reversal interval, not an internal tear. Leading/trailing stops are outside gestures. Long observed same-direction holds have no arbitrary upper-duration cutoff. Invalid/nonfinite/calibration/clock input yields an unknown result with a reason and no invented timeline.

The analysis state describes observed movement, deliberately separate from the canonical state's hand-driven assertion. `handContactUnobserved` is always retained for accepted evidence. Free running physical revolutions stay continuous movement with no wrap-induced reversal or tear; position alone cannot prove release or hand control. The API has no fader argument and returns no scratch identifier/name or `GestureRecord.tearLabel`. No app consumer, authoring/training eligibility, persistence, export schema, UI, resources, signing settings, plist, scheme, entitlement or project file changed.

### Fixed synthetic policy and boundary evidence

All values are starting points for synthetic fixtures, NOT measured CXL calibration. Configuration must be supplied explicitly. Speed and excursion use the chosen calibration's output unit; the fixture unit is revolutions. Sample-position input needs independently justified equivalent thresholds.

| Parameter | Synthetic value |
| --- | --- |
| Enter moving / stationary speed | 0.08 / 0.02 units per second |
| Minimum moving / hold duration | 40 / 40 ms |
| Maximum repair duration | 20 ms, strictly below both minimum durations |
| Maximum jitter / stationary excursion | 0.0005 / 0.001 units |
| Minimum sample rate | 100 Hz; enforced per pair, not mean rate |
| Maximum sample gap | 50 ms; gaps over 10 ms are already degraded at 100 Hz |
| Maximum plausible speed | 8 units per second |
| Minimum input confidence | 0.8, with valid range through 1 |

Duration and speed thresholds are inclusive with `1e-9` arithmetic tolerance. Tests bracket 40 ms minimum durations at 39/40/41 ms, repairs at 19/20/21 ms plus an intentional 40 ms hold, jitter excursion at 0.00049/0.00050/0.00051, moving speed at 0.07999/0.08000/0.08001, stationary speed at 0.01999/0.02000/0.02001, sample rate at 99/100/101 Hz (plus 25/50 Hz), and the gap limit at 49/50/51 ms. Sample-aligned synthetic boundaries are pinned within `1e-9` seconds; off-grid boundaries allow one sample period at 100/200/400 Hz. Reported boundary resolution is the largest sample pair incident to that boundary, not a statistical confidence interval or a guarantee for gradual acceleration.

Fixtures cover baby turnaround with/without a stop, 1/2/3 tears (162 combinations of direction, rate, speed and hold length per test-plan configuration), unequal moving ratios, slow drag, intentional long hold, jitter near zero/spikes, quick/sub-minimum reversal, dropped events, multiple free-running revolutions, unit/origin/sign transformations, malformed clocks, sparse samples, bad confidence, implausible jumps and deterministic coverage. No physical performance was used to tune the policy.

### False positives and calibration still required

Position alone cannot distinguish an intentional tear from an incidental same-direction pause, braking, or a stall; output is a motion candidate only. Very slow drift inside both the speed and excursion deadbands can appear stationary. A device that repeats stale positions at fresh timestamps can look like a hold without separate freshness evidence. Wraps/cue jumps that remain below the plausible-speed ceiling can look like real movement. The source must provide continuous, actually observed coordinates and a trustworthy monotonic clock.

A real hold/reversal below the configured temporal resolution may be merged only as low-confidence jitter or left unknown. Even a short bounded bridged gap could hide such a movement; it never earns a measured ratio. Long or ambiguous gaps reduce recall intentionally. Gradual accelerations shift threshold crossings, so one-sample fixture tolerance is not physical timing accuracy.

Real CXL calibration must establish physical/sample-position scale, forward sign and cue origin; live cadence and freshness semantics; timestamp jitter/gaps and clock behavior; speed noise near zero; usable slow-drag range; displacement drift/quantization; shortest reliably observed intentional hold/reversal across performers and tempi; maximum credible movement/cue-jump separation; and the meaning of input confidence. Validate the thresholds, excursion limits, minimum durations, repair budget, sample-rate/gap limits and confidence cutoff against multiple held-out performances. No physical calibration, capture, named-technique recognition, authoring approval or training claim is made.

Reference artifacts/session/evidence carry the derived companion; Review preserves it and requires continuous measured stillness bounded by same-direction travel for automatic holds. The original guard covered clock-conflicted travel spans but missed transition-only discontinuities; the Prompt A follow-up corrects that omission. Fader evidence never supplies structure. Historical movement events and raw packets remain verbatim; the companion is rebuilt on read through the existing decoder, not a new persisted/export schema. Old lost travel is explicitly marked discarded/unknown rather than rewriting historical evidence.

# 2026-09-06 — Take 008 `crossfaderTakeStartState` correction: absent field, not recorded unknown (read-only evidence audit)

Correcting a characterisation only. No historical line above is rewritten, no artifact was modified, and Take 008's recorded fingerprint (55 platter movement events, 19,097 mixer MIDI events, ZERO mapped crossfader samples, linked Watch capture `786056BA-4C08-4277-9422-43FE0BF88E2D`, completed/manual stop) stands unchanged and correct.

A working note in the parked-fader recovery brief stated that Take 008's `crossfaderTakeStartState` "existed but was unknown". The artifact does not support that. Read read-only from `~/Library/Containers/com.machelpnz.scratchlab/Data/Library/Application Support/ScratchLab/RoutineCaptures/41949897-5458-449d-9280-65508a4f6600_take008_routine.json`, the top-level key `crossfaderTakeStartState` is ABSENT.

Three states must not be conflated:

- **Absent key** — no `crossfaderTakeStartState` in the JSON. `CaptureCore.swift` declares it as an `Optional` on `LocalRecordingSidecar` with synthesized `Codable` and no custom `CodingKeys`, so `JSONEncoder` omits it when nil. Absent is therefore indistinguishable from, and equivalent to, nil.
- **Decoded nil** — what an absent key becomes on read. `ReferenceCrossfaderTakeStart.correlate` maps it with `guard let state else { return .rejected(.notRecorded) }`, i.e. `.notRecorded`.
- **Recorded unknown** — a NON-nil record whose `provenance == .unknown` and whose `unknownReason` is populated. It serialises as a PRESENT key and maps to a different rejection, `.recordedUnknown`.

Take 008 is the first case. The timing settles why: it was recorded `startedAt 2026-09-05T21:45:42Z` (2026-09-06 09:45 NZST), whereas the field was introduced by `d0e9ac6` authored 2026-09-06T16:36:42+12:00 — roughly six hours and fifty minutes AFTER the recording. The code path that emits an explicit `unknown` did not exist when Take 008 was written, so the field could not have been populated at all. This is exactly the case the field's own doc comment anticipates: "a sidecar written before this field existed decodes as `nil`, meaning 'not recorded'."

Consequence for the parked-fader work: Take 008 remains valid evidence for the zero-mapped-crossfader/parked-fader SHAPE, but it is NOT evidence of an `unknown` take-start classification and must not be cited as such. The connection-generation defect it was invoked to justify is established independently, from the code path and deterministic regression tests, not from this artifact.

No take was recorded, parsed for training, altered, approved, exported, installed, published or promoted. Production container file count unchanged at 954 with no modification in the audit window.

## 2026-09-06 (Prompt C — coordinate contract and Review truth)

Worktree `/Users/karlwatson/Downloads/ScratchLab-TTM-Reconstruct`, branch `feature/ttm-crossfader-takestart-reconstruct`, base `9bb82d1` (Prompt B, `fix(capture): preserve parked fader state and calibration status`), whose ancestors include Prompt A `cb4adc5` and the camera repair `63e2898`. Began with a clean worktree and empty index; nothing was pre-existing dirty, so the whole candidate is this slice.

Root cause of the audited mismatch, pinned to two lines. `CaptureCore.decodePlatterCore` comments its own step 3 as "Normalize the integrated position to 0…1 over the stream's range" and writes those fractions into every `DetectedNotationRecordMovementEvent` it emits with `source: "controller"`. Finalization persists exactly those events, `ReferenceAuthoringCaptureBridge` hands them to `ReferenceTakeEvidence.platterMovementEvents`, and `ReferenceTearSegmentationReviewBuilder.build(for:)` segments them. `ReferenceTearCanonicalProjectionBuilder` then stamped every produced `ScratchNotation.GestureRecord` with a hardcoded `static let coordinateSpace = .platterRevolutions`. Span-normalised take-local fractions were therefore handed to a record whose declared space said revolutions. The LIVE path reaches the same projection from `derivePlatterMovementEventsWithProvisional`, which divides raw CC6 step displacement by `PlatterCoordinateSemantics.raneOneMKIIDirectMIDIStepsPerRevolution` (3,600) and genuinely is revolutions. Two different divisors, one constant label.

Decision. `ScratchNotation.GestureRecord.CoordinateSpace` gains a third case, `normalizedTakeLocalDisplacement`. `CaptureCore.PlatterNotationCoordinates` is the named contract: a `Basis` (`calibratedPlatterRevolutions` / `normalizedTakeLocalDisplacement`) plus a non-empty `reference` string stating what established it. Every default is the NON-CLAIMING basis, so a forgotten argument can only understate the claim; `calibratedRevolutions(stepsPerRevolution:reference:)` returns `nil` for a non-finite, non-positive or unreferenced divisor, and `raneOneMKIIDirectMIDI(stepsPerRevolution:)` fails closed to take-local with the reason stated rather than claiming a revolution it cannot support. The review stores the basis; the projection reads `review.platterCoordinates.coordinateSpace` and emits `.gestureLocalPlatterRevolutions` or the new `.gestureLocalNormalizedDisplacement` accordingly. `build(for: evidence)` states `.normalizedTakeLocal()` explicitly, and `.uncalibratedPlatterCoordinates` is now appended only when the basis really is uncalibrated.

The finalized reference path declares NORMALIZED, not revolutions. Calibrated revolutions are not "genuinely available" there: `ReferenceTakeEvidence` carries no raw mixer MIDI and no steps-per-revolution reference, so any revolution claim would have to be fabricated. Feeding the presentation re-derivation into the review instead would change the displacement magnitudes the unchanged review thresholds are expressed in, which is segmentation tuning and was out of scope. `LivePerformedNotationTracker.platterCoordinates` declares the calibrated basis at the boundary that knows which branch of `computeState` ran, and falls back to the non-claiming basis for the camera branch; `ReferenceAuthoringView` passes it through. `source` alone can never settle the unit, because an identically-sourced `"controller"` event is calibrated live and span-normalised once persisted.

Live/finalized parity is established on time, grid, direction and hold structure, with positions agreeing exactly once each is rescaled onto its own span — which is what `ScratchStrokeGeometry.CanonicalFrame` does at draw time. Both bases are linear in raw steps with a constant positive divisor, so the drawn shape is identical while the declared unit is not. A record whose space differs from the frame's still renders as explicit MOTION UNKNOWN and acquires no hold; contrary-direction curves still render UNKNOWN and manufacture no horizontal Tear hold. No detection threshold, noise gate, hold-ambiguity policy or segmentation parameter was touched.

Review truth. `ReferenceAuthoringViewModel.advisoryDetectionStatement(for:)` replaces the "(does not match CXL selection)" warning. `MacScratchDetector.process` runs one matcher, `matchBabyScratch`, hardcoding `baby_scratch`, and `ScratchClassifying` registers only `BabyScratchClassifier`, so the detector cannot express Tear at all; on a Tear-selected take its Baby Scratch result is now labelled LIMITED and is explicitly not a disagreement, while a mismatch inside the detector's real vocabulary still reads as one. It never writes `evidence.metadata.technique`. Review overload is reduced by grouping and lazy disclosure only: `tearCandidateGroups` is a strict partition of `review.candidates` carrying candidate IDs, deleting nothing and asserting no classification, and only the decision-worthy buckets open by default. `tearCoordinateContractText` states the unit on the evidence summary so no operator has to guess whether a number is a revolution.

CODEX CHANGES IN THIS CONTINUATION. Append compares the complete ticket, including owner, generation, epoch and optional token. The single generation also supplies each armed token's unique value, removing the extra token sequence. The token carries its immutable media URL so a delegate may acquire only the token for that recording; that same token crosses the asynchronous audio/mux and finalization stages. Both finalization stages refuse stale tokens, and a mismatched drain returns without continuing finalization. Arming refuses an undrained take; the real start entry point refuses it before changing camera/duration/sidecar/audio state, and the catch abandons only the optional token actually obtained by that start. Epoch open/close also require a matching token. Existing preview/time retention behavior is retained. The view keeps its plain-let engine, @State presentation fields, and one tracker constructor; its onReceive handler and lifecycle transition now share directly executable functions with the tests. Replayed, duplicate and stale release counts are ignored, and off/take presentation modes cannot re-arm a preview. Three existing capture regressions now explicitly arm and open real take windows.

FINAL INVARIANT. One `midiCaptureLock` owns idle/preview/take, one monotonically increasing generation, the epoch, one optional unique take token, and the existing event array. A take token exists exactly under take ownership. Real `receiveMIDIPacketList` captures one whole ticket under that lock and carries it through parsing/dispatch; immediately before append the same lock validates ALL ticket fields, rejects idle and epoch zero, calculates takeRelativeTime solely from the ticket epoch, and appends atomically. No caller epoch parameter exists. Arming clears preview events before establishing a take epoch. Stop closes admission but retains take ownership/evidence. Only a matching drain or abandonment transitions take to idle and publishes one release on DispatchQueue.main, after unlocking. Stale/duplicate operations publish nothing. isRoutineRecording/isRoutineFinalizationPending are not MIDI ownership authorities; the existing finalization-pending gate still separately protects the wider recording pipeline until sidecar finalization finishes.

RETENTION. Preview only: provisional 15-second trailing retention, existing amortized trim trigger at a 30-second held span, strict maximum 32,000 held events, and a 24,000-event count-trim target. Min/max timestamps handle out-of-order arrivals; trimming filters by timestamp rather than dropping an assumed-old prefix. The 15-second policy is not a claim of an exact 15-second post-append span: the retained amortization allows up to 30 seconds between trims. Idle expiry occurs only on a later append that triggers trimming; there is no timer expiry. The real append tests reach 32,000, 32,001 and 33,000 preview arrivals (final held count 24,999), and a take retains/drains all 33,000 events exactly once.
